title: INVESTORLAR VA MANFAATDOR TOMONLARNING FAOLLIGI HAMDA ULARNI KOMPANIYA BOSHQARUVIGA JALB QILISH SHAKLLARI
summary: Mazkur ilmiy ishda investorlar va manfaatdor tomonlarning kompaniya boshqaruviga faol ishtirok etishining nazariy asoslari, amaliy mexanizmlari va iqtisodiy oqibatlarini keng ko`lamda tahlil qiladi. Aksiyadorlik faolligi, institutsional investorlarning ovoz berish huquqlari, ijtimoiy mas'uliyat talablari va ESG (atrof-muhit, ijtimoiy va boshqaruv) mezonlari bo'yicha mavjud adabiyotlar tizimli ravishda ko'rib chiqilgan. Tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, faol investorlarning kompaniya qarorlariga ta'siri nafaqat moliyaviy samaradorlikni oshiradi, balki korporativ shaffoflik, boshqaruv sifati va uzoq muddatli barqarorlikni ham sezilarli darajada yaxshilaydi. Ushbu munosabat, ayniqsa, rivojlanayotgan bozor kontekstida o'rganilganda, samarali boshqaruv mexanizmlari, qonuniy tartibga solish muhiti va manfaatdor tomonlar o'rtasidagi muloqot sifatiga bog'liqligi aniqlangan. Maqolada, shuningdek, xedj-fondlar faolligi, proksi-maslahat firmalari va institutsional investorlarning ovoz berish amaliyotlari alohida tahlil qilinadi. Xulosalar shuni tasdiqlaydiki, investorlar va manfaatdor tomonlarning kompaniya boshqaruviga samarali jalb qilinishi strategik muloqot, tartibga solish islohotlari va boshqaruv madaniyatining shakllanishi orqali erishiladi.

title: When and How Firms Can Promote Green Innovation for Sustainable Development: A Holistic Examination
summary: Green finance has become a key instrument for addressing environmental degradation and supporting sustainable development. However, existing literature has largely focused on its outcomes, with limited attention to the factors that contribute to its effectiveness. Using an input-oriented perspective, this study examines the roles of green innovation, financial development, and research and development (R&D) in promoting green financing and sustainable development. Empirical data from thirty-nine manufacturing companies in Saudi Arabia covering 2011–2025 are analyzed using partial least squares, generalized method of moments, fixed-effects, and random-effects models. The findings demonstrate that green innovation, financial development, and R&D significantly contribute to the effectiveness of green financing. The transition from conventional product innovation to green finance is found to be less challenging than the development of eco-friendly technological innovations, as environmentally friendly products can generate positive financial returns. The study provides policy insights for promoting sustainable industrial growth.

title: THE PERIPHERAL PLACE OF SUSTAINABILITY IN THE AGENDA AND PROFESSIONAL LEGACY OF BRAZILIAN CFOS
summary: Objectives: To examine whether sustainability is central or peripheral in the agenda and legacy of Chief Financial Officers of large Brazilian firms, read against the attributes of responsible leadership. Theoretical framework: The study draws on responsible leadership theory, upper echelons theory and the institutional account of symbolic and substantive adoption known as decoupling. Method: A cross sectional survey of 106 CFOs of large Brazilian firms was analysed with descriptive statistics, comparing the prioritised ESG pillar, the weekly agenda for sustainability and technology, the professional legacy and the ethical self assessment. Results and discussion: Technology took more of the weekly agenda than sustainability, 21.1% against 15.2%. ESG was read as governance by 77.4%, against 16.0% environmental and 6.6% social, and sustainability figured in none of the legacies CFOs would leave. Ethics was rated high by 80.2% yet rested on conduct rather than structures. The finance apex enacts the individual attributes of responsible leadership and leaves the systemic ones symbolic. Research implications: Advancing the Sustainable Development Goals inside firms depends less on endorsement than on moving sustainability from a professed value to an operative priority and from governance towards the environmental and social dimensions. Originality and value: The study relocates the symbolic and substantive distinction from firm disclosure to the finance leader's stated agenda, with emerging economy evidence on a role the literature has overlooked.

title: Building Africa's Digital & AI Foundation: Data Infrastructure & Trust
summary: Building Africa's Digital Foundation: Data, Infrastructure and Trust is the inaugural whitepaper in a thought leadership series exploring the forces shaping Africa's digital and artificial intelligence future. Written from the perspective of a telecommunications and data transformation leader, the paper argues that Africa's next era of economic growth will be built on the strategic combination of digital infrastructure, data, and trust. Drawing on examples from Ghana and across the African continent, the paper examines how connectivity, cloud platforms, digital identity systems, fintech innovation, artificial intelligence, and modern data ecosystems are becoming the foundational layers of a new digital economy. Positioned at the intersection of technology, business strategy, and public policy, the paper presents a framework for policymakers, business executives, technology leaders, and development practitioners seeking to accelerate digital transformation while ensuring that growth remains inclusive, ethical, and economically meaningful. As the first publication in a broader series, Leading Africa's Digital & AI Future, it establishes the central thesis that Africa's digital future will be determined not only by the technologies it adopts, but by the institutions, governance structures, talent ecosystems, and trust frameworks it builds around them. Subsequent papers expand on these themes by examining the evolution from digital foundations to data intelligence, artificial intelligence, digital leadership, and the future of value creation in African organizations.

title: Digital Transformation and Low-Carbon Transition Risk in Manufacturing Firms: A Green Innovation Perspective
summary: Promoting the digital transformation of manufacturing and reducing the risks of the low-carbon transition are necessary steps to achieve carbon peaking and neutrality goals and drive all-round green development. Using publicly listed manufacturing enterprises in China from 2010 to 2024 as the research sample, this paper empirically examines the effect of digital transformation on corporate vulnerability to low-carbon transition and identifies the corresponding transmission paths. Digital transformation will reduce the risk of the low-carbon transition for manufacturing companies. Green innovation provides a necessary path for digital transformation to mitigate the aforementioned risk. After adding another category to the classification of innovation drivers, this study found that substantive green innovation significantly mediated the effect, but strategic green innovation did not. Therefore, digital transformation is likely to drive high-quality substantive changes rather than a large number of symbolic ones. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the risk-reducing effect of digital transformation is more pronounced in companies with a higher proportion of skilled technical staff, chair–CEO separation and those facing looser financing constraints. The above results provide empirical support and policy references for promoting the synchronous digital-green development of manufacturing enterprises and for identifying and mitigating low-carbon transition risks.

title: Entrepreneurship-Based Green Finance Model: Optimizing the Role of Regional-Owned Enterprises (BUMD) in Achieving Jakarta’s Net Zero Emission 2060 Target
summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of willingness to innovate, proactive attitude, and risk-taking propensity on green finance and sustainability performance among Regional-Owned Enterprises (BUMD) in DKI Jakarta. The research employs a quantitative method using Structural Equation Modeling with Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) analysis, based on primary survey data collected from 23 BUMDs in Jakarta in 2025. The findings reveal that willingness to innovate and proactive attitude positively contribute to strengthening green finance; however, only the proactive attitude consistently enhances sustainability performance. Conversely, the willingness to take risks shows a negative effect on green finance and an insignificant impact on sustainability performance. Furthermore, green finance exerts a positive, though not yet significant, influence on sustainability performance. These findings underscore the need for operational strategies such as strengthening green innovation, establishing sustainability teams, implementing green risk management, and developing sustainability reports as integral components of transparent and accountable governance. Such strategies are essential to reinforce the strategic role of BUMDs in supporting the transition toward a green economy and achieving Jakarta’s Net Zero Emission 2060 target.

title: The Accountability Pathway: Linking ESG Disclosure, Integrated Reporting Quality, and Value Creation in Southeast Asia
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how listed firms in Southeast Asia translate internal environmental, social, and governance (ESG) commitments into accountable practices, transparent reporting, and organizational value creation. Focusing on firms in the ASEAN‐6 countries over the period 2020–2024, the study proposes and empirically tests a framework in which ESG disclosure enhances integrated reporting quality and, ultimately, value creation, as measured by investment efficiency, while accounting for macro‐level energy transition pressures and firm‐level corporate governance mechanisms. Using panel data from 2605 firms, the study employs maximum likelihood structural equation modeling within a moderated mediation framework, while controlling for country‐level fixed effects. The findings indicate that ESG disclosure significantly enhances integrated reporting quality and that reporting quality serves as a key mechanism through which ESG disclosure contributes to value creation. The results further demonstrate that the accountability pathway is context‐dependent: energy transition pressures strengthen the importance of sustainability accountability, whereas corporate governance influences firms' capacity to implement ESG strategies effectively. This study contributes to the literature by conceptualizing corporate social responsibility as a multistage process that links ESG knowledge, disclosure and reporting infrastructure, and value creation. The findings offer practical implications for managers, investors, and policymakers seeking to enhance corporate transparency and promote sustainable capital allocation across ASEAN economies.

title: Blockchain Management Empowering Green and Climate Finance: Mechanisms, Real‑World Dilemmas and Optimization Paths
summary: Against the background of China's dual-carbon strategic goals, green and climate finance have achieved rapid scale expansion as critical instruments for low-carbon economic transition. Nevertheless, the whole market is still plagued by prominent governance risks, including intentional environmental data manipulation, and repeated double-counting of carbon assets, as well as poor traceability of green project capital flows. As an innovative trust-rebuilding management paradigm rather than simple technical tools, blockchain management leverages distributed ledgers, data immutability and smart-contract functions to deliver credible technical support for green-climate finance. This paper adopts qualitative analytical research, including literature review and dual-case comparison, to investigate how blockchain management functions within green credit, carbon trading and green bond scenarios. It identifies major practical obstacles and puts forward coordinated institutional-technical optimization proposals. The study reveals that blockchain can effectively mitigate information asymmetry in green-financial practice. Nevertheless, its large-scale commercial deployment is hindered by on-chain-off-chain data fragmentation, insufficient unified regulatory standards and relatively high technical operation costs. Therefore, collaborative governance mechanisms, unified industry-wide standards and lower access thresholds for small- and medium-sized enterprises are urgently required for future development.

title: ESG measurement, innovation pathways, and sustainable firm value creation: A systematic review of metrics, mechanisms, and contexts
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance is increasingly linked to firm value through innovation, yet evidence remains fragmented across measurement systems, mechanisms, and contexts (Li & Sutunyarak, 2024; Widyantoro et al., 2025). This study systematically reviews how ESG is measured, which innovation pathways connect ESG to value creation, and which contextual conditions shape these relationships. Following PRISMA 2020, 60 Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed studies published between 2022 and 2026 were analyzed. The findings show that ESG ratings, composite scores, and disclosure-based indicators dominate measurement, while green innovation, technological innovation, digital transformation, research and development (R&D) intensity, and innovation capability constitute the main transmission pathways. Firm value is most frequently assessed through return on assets (ROA), return on equity (ROE), Tobin’s Q, profitability, enterprise value, and broader performance indicators. Overall, ESG is associated with favorable firm-level outcomes, but these effects depend on credible measurement, active innovation mechanisms, and supportive organizational and institutional conditions. For industry, the findings support integrating ESG with innovation capabilities; for research and academia, they highlight the need for more comparable ESG measures and context-sensitive models of sustainable value creation.

title: ASSESSMENT OF ESG REPORTING AMONG MONGOLIA’S TOP 100 COMPANIES
summary: Abstract Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting is an internationally standardized framework for assessing corporate sustainability, social responsibility, and long-term value creation. According to IBM, ESG represents an integrated framework for sustainability assessment. In Mongolia, formal regulation of ESG reporting was introduced in 2022 following the revision of the Regulation on Public Information Transparency by the Financial Regulatory Commission and the Mongolian Stock Exchange, which established mandatory disclosure requirements for ESG-related information for publicly listed companies. In parallel, the ESG Sustainability Reporting Guideline approved in 2022 has been undergoing alignment with the international IFRS S1 standard during 2024–2025. The objective of this study is to evaluate the current level of ESG disclosure among Mongolia’s TOP 100 companies as identified by the Mongolian National Chamber of Commerce and Industry in 2024. Of the TOP 100 companies, 25 firms that publicly disclosed ESG reports were selected for analysis. A total of 375 qualitative assessments were conducted across 15 indicators grouped into the three core ESG pillars—Environmental (E), Social (S), and Governance (G). Following qualitative scoring, company rankings and quantitative statistical analyses were performed using SPSS, including Ranking, One-way ANOVA, Welch and Brown–Forsythe robust tests, and post hoc comparisons. The One-way ANOVA results indicate no statistically significant differences in mean ESG scores across industry sectors (F(4,20)=0.98, p=.44). Levene’s test confirmed homogeneity of variances (p=.809), while the Welch (p=.65) and Brown–Forsythe (p=.49) robust tests similarly revealed no statistically significant inter-sectoral differences. Although the effect size (η²=.16) suggests a moderate practical effect, the absence of statistical significance may be attributable to the relatively small sample size and uneven distribution of firms across sectors. Post hoc analyses consistently grouped all sectors into a single homogeneous subset, further confirming the lack of statistically meaningful differences. The findings suggest that ESG reporting among Mongolia’s leading companies has not yet reached a level of sectoral differentiation, with systemic challenges related to data availability, reporting quality, and standard implementation remaining prevalent. Comparative analysis across ESG components shows that Environmental (E) disclosure scores highest, followed by Social (S) performance at a moderate level, while Governance (G) disclosure remains comparatively weak. As ESG reporting practices improve and data coverage expands, future research will enable more evidence-based assessments of sectoral policy implications, corporate governance quality, and social responsibility performance in Mongolia.

title: Impacting Green Finance on Sustainable Agricultural Development: Evidence from Vietnam
summary: The transition toward sustainable agriculture requires substantial financial resources aligned with environmental and social objectives. Green finance has emerged as a critical instrument for mobilizing such resources; however, the mechanisms by which institutional, technological, and market forces shape green finance and translate into sustainable agricultural development remain underexplored, particularly in emerging economies. This study investigates the determinants of green finance and its role in promoting sustainable agricultural development in Vietnam. Using a mixed-methods approach, qualitative interviews with 45 experts in green farm economics and agrarian project financing were conducted first to develop context-specific measurement scales. Subsequently, a large-scale survey of 900 respondents from farm cooperatives, agricultural enterprises, green project participants, and green supply chain actors was conducted. The proposed research model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that environmental regulation pressure is the most influential driver of green finance, followed by stakeholder and market ESG pressure and digital financial inclusion. Green finance significantly promotes sustainable agricultural development and serves as a key transmission mechanism linking institutional, technological, and market factors to sustainability outcomes. Moreover, green supply chain requirements and ESG governance and transparency significantly strengthen the effectiveness of green finance and policy instruments. This study contributes to the literature by integrating green finance, ESG governance, and supply chain perspectives into a unified framework and provides important policy implications for promoting sustainable agriculture in emerging economies.

title: Sustainable accounting and its impact on business development: A systematic review
summary: This systematic literature review (SLR) examines how sustainable accounting influences business development by synthesizing evidence from 71 articles published between 2020 and 2025 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science (WoS). The objective of this study was to analyze the influence of sustainable accounting on business development and identify the main organizational challenges, implementation strategies, and outcomes associated with its adoption. Using the PICO strategy and the PRISMA protocol, the study identifies key organizational challenges, implementation strategies, and outcomes related to sustainable accounting. The findings show that sustainable accounting strengthens business development through corporate social responsibility (CSR), sustainability reporting, environmental management accounting, technological innovation, risk management, cost efficiency, and long-term value creation. In particular, 42 percent of the reviewed studies emphasized improvements linked to social responsibility and corporate governance, while the remaining evidence highlighted financial transparency, technological innovation, and environmental accounting practices. Consistent with Schaltegger et al. (2022) and Alsarayrah et al. (2024), the review concludes that sustainable accounting is both a managerial and strategic tool for integrating economic, social, and environmental performance. The article contributes by systematizing recent evidence, identifying research gaps, and supporting the adoption of sustainable accounting practices for long-term business development.

title: Digital Procurement Capabilities and Supply Chain Resilience: Building Competitive Advantage in the Era of Digital Transformation
summary: Digital transformation has repositioned procurement from a transaction-processing function to a strategic source of information, coordination, risk intelligence and organisational adaptability. title: ESG and Profitability in the Palm Oil Industry: A Literature Review
summary: Profitability is a key indicator of performance for oil palm plantation companies, but long-term profitability is increasingly influenced by their ability to manage environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks and opportunities. This article presents a narrative literature review to develop an ESG-based sustainability model and examine its relationship with profitability, primarily proxied by Return on Assets (ROA). The Environmental dimension covers emissions reduction, biodiversity protection, land management, waste and water management, and sustainable production. The Social dimension encompasses worker welfare, occupational safety, community relations, human rights, and smallholder inclusion. The Governance dimension includes board oversight, transparency, risk management, compliance, and stakeholder accountability. The synthesis indicates that sustainability standards and early adoption can influence palm oil company performance, although financial impacts vary because ESG implementation involves costs alongside benefits such as operational efficiency, market access, reputation, and risk reduction. The proposed model positions ESG as a multidimensional strategic capability that influences profitability through operational efficiency, risk reduction, legitimacy, market access, and stakeholder trust. This article provides a conceptual foundation for future empirical testing of oil palm plantation companies without claiming statistical results from company data.

title: Investing with a conscience: the impact of ESG performance on corporate financing ease in Western Europe
summary: This study examines the impact of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance on corporate financing strategies in Western Europe, focusing on debt maturity and financing structure. Using a panel dataset of 8,592 firm-year observations from 706 listed non-financial firms during 2009–2021, the results show that stronger ESG performance is associated with longer debt maturity and greater reliance on internal financing. Mechanism analysis further indicates that improved ESG performance alleviates firms’ financing constraints, thereby reduce financing frictions. These findings suggest that strong ESG performance increases both shareholder and creditor confidence, enabling firms to secure more favorable financing conditions. Additional analysis reveals stronger effects among non-state-owned enterprises and firms with lower leverage. The findings remain robust across a battery of robustness and endogeneity tests and provide important implications for investors, corporate managers, and policymakers regarding the strategic role of ESG performance in corporate financing decisions and long-term sustainable development.

title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
summary: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. This paper critically examines Bangladesh's environmental governance architecture, the major barriers to its effective implementation, and opportunities for achieving a just green transition. It adopts a qualitative, desk-based methodology combining doctrinal legal analysis with critical examination of national policies and plans, international commitments, judicial decisions, and institutional reports. The analysis demonstrates that Bangladesh has an extensive environmental legal and policy framework, including constitutional obligations, pollution-control legislation, environmental courts, climate strategies, and long-term delta planning. However, its implementation remains constrained by fragmented institutional authority, inconsistent enforcement, inadequate monitoring capacity, weaknesses in environmental assessment procedures, limited local government capacity, and continuing incentives for environmentally harmful investments. Climate vulnerability further intensifies these governance challenges, disproportionately affecting low-income and climate-vulnerable communities. Nevertheless, significant opportunities exist for a just green transition through renewable energy, resource-efficient industries, circular production systems, nature-based adaptation, sustainable agriculture, green finance, and digitally enabled environmental accountability. The paper proposes a reform agenda centred on enforceable environmental standards, strategic environmental assessment, open environmental data, stronger institutional coordination, enhanced local capacity, effective application of the polluter-pays principle, and meaningful public participation. Sustainable development in Bangladesh will become credible only when environmental protection becomes a binding condition of development decision-making rather than a remedial response after environmental damage has occurred.

title: What Counts as a Community Grievance? Delimitation, Dissent and Distortion in a Company’s Human Rights Mechanism in Kenya
summary: Abstract Operational-level grievance mechanisms are often viewed as a means to empower rightsholders to access remedy for human rights abuses. This article presents qualitative research findings on Kakuzi’s ‘Independent Human Rights Mechanism’, a mechanism specifically designed to provide remedy for human rights abuses. Kakuzi’s grievance mechanism takes place in the context of historical land injustices, whereby thousands of squatters are subject to practices of enclosure—territorial, legal and epistemic—that legitimate Kakuzi’s authority over the land. The article takes an actor-oriented approach, following grievances across their full trajectory—from community members’ injurious experience, to those grievances heard by the mechanism, to representation of community grievances in corporate disclosure—while foregrounding the agency communities exercise in relation to the mechanism. The mechanism delimits which grievances are admissible and remediable. Communities dissent from this delimitation through various strategies. Corporate disclosure of grievances then distorts local realities.

title: INVESTMENT ATTRACTIVENESS OF THE COMMUNICATIONS SECTOR OF UKRAINE AS THE BASIS OF ITS SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
summary: The article examines the investment attractiveness of Ukraine’s communications (electronic communications) sector as a key prerequisite for ensuring its sustainable development under martial law and post-war recovery conditions. Special attention is paid to the analysis of the dynamics and structure of capital investments in the sector, factors of the investment climate and the relationship between investment activity and the sustainable development of the industry. Based on data from the National Commission for the State Regulation of Electronic Communications (NCEC) and surveys of the European Business Association, it has been established that in 2022–2025 capital investments in electronic communications increased from UAH 12.6 to 33.9 billion. The main barriers and incentives for investment activity have been identified. Directions for increasing the investment attractiveness of the industry are proposed, taking into account the goals of sustainable development and European integration processes. The study reveals that despite significant security risks and infrastructure damage caused by the full-scale war, the telecommunications sector of Ukraine has shown remarkable resilience. Capital expenditures increased by more than 30% annually in 2024–2025, reflecting operators’ commitment to network restoration, resilience enhancement (backup power solutions), and preparation for 5G deployment. The investment climate index of Ukraine improved to 2.70 points in 2025 according to the EBA survey, approaching pre-war levels. Positive factors include European integration progress, digitalization of public services, and preferential trade regimes. Key challenges remain related to security risks, regulatory uncertainty, energy supply instability, and the need for large-scale reconstruction of damaged infrastructure. The article substantiates that increasing investment attractiveness of the communications sector is a fundamental condition for achieving sustainable development goals, ensuring digital inclusion, supporting economic recovery, and strengthening national resilience. Practical recommendations include improvement of the regulatory framework, development of public-private partnership mechanisms, stimulation of foreign direct investment through risk insurance instruments, acceleration of 5G spectrum allocation, and integration of ESG principles into investment strategies of telecom operators. The research also highlights the critical role of telecommunications infrastructure in supporting Ukraine’s digital transformation agenda and the country’s integration into the European Digital Single Market.

title: Impacts of Edge AI/agentic AI on supply chain management and operations research
summary: Abstract Edge AI refers to the deployment and execution of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms on decentralized, local computing devices (e.g., Internet of Things) rather than relying on centralized cloud‐based computing infrastructures. The literature has addressed the increasing importance of AI in supply chain and operations management (SCOM), specifically in learning‐based, generative, and agentic AI, as well as digital twins. However, the area of Edge AI has not yet received a theoretical framing and conceptualization in SCOM. In this paper, we discuss the impacts of Edge AI on SCOM. We begin with an analysis of AI in SCOM, focusing on learning‐based, generative, agentic AI, and digital twins. We then detail Edge AI's impacts on SCOM across Digital SCOR functions: orchestration, fulfillment and ordering, planning, sourcing, regeneration, synchronization, and transformation. We also analyze organizational transformations that Edge AI might trigger. Specifically, we discuss interactions of agentic AI and Edge AI, an integration of local and centralized decision‐making, and deployment scenarios of Edge AI use in SCOM, focusing on production planning and control, intralogistics, and supply chain resilience. Risks and challenges of the new technology are considered as well. Impacts of Edge AI on supply chain and operations research are discussed. We conclude that Edge AI is a crucial part of the unfolding Industry 6.0 revolution that, in combination with agentic AI, provides a technology to implement decentralized, autonomously planned and controlled supply chain, production, and logistics processes, materializing in Industry 6.0 with AI across all layers of value‐added chains.

title: Can the digital economy enhance urban ecological environment resilience?
summary: Based on city-level panel data of China from 2006 to 2022, this study develops comprehensive indicator system for urban ecological environment resilience, and derives the composite development index of urban ecological environment resilience via the entropy method. To identify the causal impact of the digital economy on urban ecological environment resilience and disentangle its core transmission mechanisms, we adopt a suite of rigorous econometric approaches, including a panel fixed effects model, quantile regression, mediation effect analysis, instrumental variable (IV) estimation and a difference-in-differences (DID) framework. Our key findings are summarised below: (1) Our baseline results show that digital economy development exerts a significant positive effect on urban ecological environment resilience, a finding that holds up to a battery of robustness checks and endogeneity corrections. (2) Further analysis reveals that the marginal empowerment effect of the digital economy varies dynamically across different stages of ecological environment resilience development, and that the impact of the digital economy features significant heterogeneity by geographic region, development stage and city size. (3) Mechanism tests identify green technology innovation, industrial structure upgrading and enhanced environmental governance capacity as the core channels through which the digital economy boosts ecological environment resilience. (4) We also document that while the digital economy improves overall ecological environment resilience levels, it does not significantly reduce regional disparities in resilience. This study enriches the theoretical body of work in related fields, and provides actionable policy insights for cities to leverage digital transformation to strengthen ecological environment resilience.

title: BUILDING A GREEN DIGITAL ECONOMY: HOW FINTECH STRENGTHENS GREEN FINANCE AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
summary: The research methodology used in this study was quantitative research design, which aimed at studying the role of fintech in strengthening the financial performance of green finance in the framework of a green digital economy. The study employed panel data of 30 countries in developing and emerging economies from 2015 to 2024, data was drawn from World Bank and IEA, financial and environmental databases. The indicators used to assess the development of fintech were digital financial services, digital payments and the adoption of financial technology, while green finance indicators were green investment, green credit and financial flows oriented towards the environment. Return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE) were used to determine financial performance. The concept of green finance was considered as a potential intervening variable that affects the financial performance of financial institutions. The controlled variables were the economic growth, inflation, foreign direct investment, financial development, and renewable energy consumption. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were conducted followed by panel regression analysis to evaluate the direct connection between fintech development and financial performance, while a mediation analysis was used to test whether green finance was a mediator to enhance the direct relationship. The diagnostic tests for multicollinearity, heteroskedasticity, cross sectional dependence and serial correlation were performed and robust standard errors were used as appropriate. The results showed that the relationship between fintech development and financial performance was positive and significant, while green finance played the role of a mediator, but it did not completely mediate the relationship between fintech development and financial performance. Green finance was shown to be a significant and partial mediation variable, and fintech development was significantly and positively associated with green finance. These results were validated in robustness tests based on alternative indicators of financial performance and fintech. These findings highlight that fintech can have an impact on the financial performance, but also through greater access to green finance channels via the allocation of funds to green activities, making green finance a potential meaningful supplement to fintech-related financial development. Policy implications are discussed.

title: Explainable AI and ESG analytics for sustainable investment decision: the roles of ESG forecast credibility and trust in AI-generated information
summary: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming sustainable investing, yet limited evidence explains how AI capabilities influence investors stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Methods This study develops and empirically tests a sequential behavioural framework explaining how AI-related characteristics influence investors stated sustainable investment preferences through perceived ESG forecast credibility and trust in AI-generated ESG information, using survey data from 566 middle-income retail investors across four Indian metropolitan cities. Results The findings reveal that explainable AI and ESG analytics capability significantly enhance perceived ESG forecast credibility, which sequentially strengthens trust in AI-generated ESG information and is associated with stronger stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Perceived Greenwashing Risk weakens the positive relationship between Perceived ESG Forecast Credibility and Trust in AI-generated ESG Information, while the interaction between Human-AI Interaction Competency and Trust in AI-generated ESG Information is statistically significant but negligible in practical magnitude (f 2 = 0.012) in relation to Sustainable Investment Decision. Discussion The study provides actionable guidance for AI developers, financial institutions, and policymakers to enhance transparency, credibility, investor trust, and responsible AI-enabled sustainable finance.

title: Microplastic contamination in agricultural systems: impacts on plant productivity, economic losses, and supply chain resilience
summary: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. This review synthesizes evidence to construct an integrated narrative that links the entry of MPs into farmland with declining plant productivity, quantifiable economic losses, and the erosion of agricultural supply chain resilience. The synthesis is based on a documented search of Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar covering January 2018 to March 2026, with explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria reported in Section 1.1. Sources, fate and soil-phase processes are treated in condensed form, because they are already covered comprehensively elsewhere; we retain only the evidence that propagates into crop, economic and supply-chain outcomes. Building on these soil-level disturbances, we evaluate the phytotoxic consequences for crops, spanning inhibited germination, impaired root architecture, reduced photosynthetic efficiency, disrupted nutrient acquisition, and the uptake and translocation of nano-sized particles into edible tissues. A central contribution of this review is the explicit coupling of these biophysical impacts to their economic and systemic dimensions, because recent global meta-analyses estimate that MP-induced photosynthetic suppression alone may reduce staple crop production by tens to hundreds of millions of tons annually, translating into substantial revenue losses, quality downgrading, remediation expenditure, and heightened exposure of food supply chains to shocks. Rather than reporting these modelled outputs at face value, we dissect the inferential chain that produces them, from effect size to biomass to harvestable yield to price, and we identify the assumptions at each step that determine whether the resulting figures are decision-grade. We complement the global estimates with farm-level cost–benefit evidence showing that the private returns to plasticulture remain positive while the contamination externality contributes under one percent of the accounted benefits of current management, which explains the persistence of practices that degrade the productive base. Throughout, illustrative case studies from China, Chile, Australia, and Europe are embedded within each thematic section rather than treated in isolation, demonstrating how local contamination patterns propagate into landscape- and market-scale consequences. We further appraise mitigation and remediation options, ranging from source reduction and material substitution to biochar amendment, and we assess emerging governance instruments such as the FAO Voluntary Code of Conduct and circular-economy regulation. Finally, we identify persistent knowledge gaps concerning the calibration of field-realistic dose–response relationships, the construction of decision-grade economic estimates, and the severe geographical imbalance of the evidence base, in which South Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America are collectively represented by a small fraction of published field studies, and we outline research priorities to safeguard soil health and food security. The review argues that microplastic contamination should be reframed not merely as an ecotoxicological problem but as a slow-onset stressor with strategic implications for the stability of global food systems.

title: STRENGTHENING U.S. PHARMACEUTICAL SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED POLICY AND REGULATORY REFORM
summary: The resilience of the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain has become a central concern for healthcare continuity, economic security, and public policy. Drug shortages expose a system in which manufacturing concentration, upstream dependencies, low-margin markets, incomplete supply-chain visibility, procurement incentives, and regulatory constraints can interact to convert localized disruptions into prolonged access problems. This narrative policy review critically examines the structural, economic, operational, and regulatory determinants of pharmaceutical supply vulnerability in the United States and evaluates the limitations of current policy responses. It argues that shortage management and supply-chain resilience are related but distinct objectives: the former is predominantly reactive, whereas the latter depends on the capacity to anticipate, absorb, adapt to, and recover from disruption. Building on this distinction, the review develops an integrated resilience architecture organized around eight functions: Detect, Assess, Incentivize, Diversify, Buffer, Adapt, Recover, and Learn. The framework links predictive supply-chain intelligence with resilience-oriented procurement, targeted manufacturing support, adaptive regulation, strategic capacity, and continuous learning. The central policy implication is that durable resilience requires coordination across regulatory, procurement, manufacturing, economic, and emergency-preparedness functions rather than a series of isolated shortage interventions. The paper therefore reframes pharmaceutical resilience as a designed property of market governance: one that must preserve safety, quality, affordability, and efficiency while reducing the probability that foreseeable vulnerabilities become prolonged national shortages.

title: Digital transformation of wafer fabrication process: a case of semiconductor manufacturing
summary: Semiconductors are essential for the digital revolution, modern electronics, and global economic growth. However, the growing demand, geopolitical tensions, and supply chain disruptions have accelerated the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology (DT) in semiconductor manufacturing. To address this gap, we studied five use cases from leading semiconductor manufacturers (Intel, Micron, Sony, Samsung, and SK Hynix). We investigate the application of AI & DT in the semiconductor wafer fabrication process (WFP). We propose a three-layer framework for WFP, consisting of supply chain, manufacturing process, and AI & DT layers, with enabling technologies. The framework incorporates AI & DT into manufacturing process-specific applications, including pattern classification, smart sensors & automation, real-time monitoring, yield prediction, automated material handling systems, predictive maintenance, data integrity, and fault & anomaly detection in semiconductor manufacturing. The implementation of AI & DT in the semiconductor industry has demonstrated significant improvements, including a 35% reduction in quality events (defects) and 25-40% reductions in cycle time. The proposed framework provides a strategy to improve operational efficiency at WFP while overcoming the limitations of the traditional approach. Key research findings highlight the potential impact of leveraging AI & DT in semiconductor WFP.

title: A Study of Artificial Intelligence and Green Finance: Building A Sustainable Economy
summary: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Green Finance have emerged as two of the most important forces that have the potential to drive the world towards a sustainable economy. The current paper attempts to explore the role of AI and Green Finance in promoting and supporting a sustainable economy with reference to building a Viksit Bharat 2047. A survey was conducted among 160 respondents, with the results analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation, regression, and an independent-samples t-test. The results demonstrated that the population studied had a generally positive perception about how AI can support Green Finance and lead the economy towards sustainability. The analysis identified strong awareness about AI as the biggest predictor of increased perception of the integration of AI and Green Finance (r = 0.78, p < .001). Additionally, participants who were aware of Green Finance had significantly higher scores for the perceived level of integration than those who were not (t = 2.65, p = .009). As such, there is reason to reject the null hypothesis, which claimed that there is no connection between the two concepts. Finally, the paper provides recommendations that financial institutions, regulators, and educators can consider in order to promote and support responsible and AI-enabled Green Finance.

title: ESG disclosure intensity and firm performance: Empirical evidence from ASEAN listed firms
summary: This study examines the association between ESG disclosure scores and firm financial performance. Firms are categorized into low- and high-ESG disclosure groups, and the study also examines the association of these categories with financial performance. The study’s independent variables are the ESG disclosure score and level groups, while the dependent variable, financial performance, is measured using Return on Assets (ROA) and Tobin’s Q. This study analyses 4,220 firm-year observations from ASEAN-listed firms using a panel fixed-effect regression. The results show that the ESG disclosure score is negatively associated with both ROA and Tobin’s Q. High-disclosure firms exhibit lower financial performance, whereas low-disclosure firms exhibit higher ROA relative to the reference group. Robustness tests using an alternative performance measure, lagged disclosure, and dynamic-panel GMM are conducted. The dynamic-panel GMM supports the negative associations with Tobin’s Q. However, the associations are no longer statistically significant when year fixed effects are included, indicating that the findings are sensitive to this specification. The negative associations appear to operate through regional temporal patterns rather than firm-level differences in disclosure. Furthermore, the study does not establish causality, and further research could examine the causal relationship between ESG disclosure and financial performance.

title: Tinjauan Literature Sistematis: Dampak Transformasi Digital terhadap Kinerja ESG
summary: Digital transformation significantly impacts various aspects of life, including the business and financial sectors. There are concept that is gaining popularity in the business world is Digitalization and ESG, which emphasizes the importance of digital, environmental, social, and corporate governance factors in investment decisions. In this context, ESG performance is crucial for determining a company's sustainability and long-term value. This study utilizes a literature review with a bibliometric analysis approach. The findings reveal that research in fintech, ESG, and digital transformation are interconnected and integrated. However, compared to other financial topics, this area remains relatively under-researched, particularly concerning ESG in SMEs.

title: Post-pandemic strategic evaluation of food supply chains using hybrid decision models
summary: The increasing complexity and disruptions in global food supply chains (FSCs), particularly after COVID-19, have emphasized the need for resilient and adaptive strategies. This study conducts a comparative analysis of various FSC structures, such as Centralized, Decentralized, Digitalized, Localized, and Hybrid models. The comparison was carried out by applying two integrated multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods: Entropy-based MOORA and Entropy-based MARCOS. Objective weights for the eight criteria (cost, flexibility, resilience, lead time, sustainability, service level, innovation capability, and risk management) were assigned through the Entropy method that was used to reduce the subjective bias. In general, both methods identified the Digitalized and Hybrid supply chain models as the two highest-ranked alternatives, while the Centralized model ranked last. To make the findings even more robust, we carried out a sensitivity analysis where we changed the criterion weights in different scenarios. Moreover, an Entropy-based COPRAS method was employed for the robustness analysis, and the findings supported the stability and consistency of the rankings across different methodological approaches. By comparing two MCDM methods in a post-pandemic context, the study contributes to the literature while offering practical guidance for stakeholders on investing in digital infrastructure, adopting hybrid supply chain models, and integrating sustainability objectives into supply chain planning. The findings provide practical guidance for policymakers and executives seeking to enhance the resilience and environmental sustainability of FSCs amid global uncertainty.

title: AI governance and digital transformation in hospitality firms: a PRISMA-based systematic review and bibliometric analysis
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation are reshaping hospitality operations, yet governance mechanisms ensuring accountability, transparency, data stewardship, and responsible innovation remain fragmented. This study systematically reviews literature on AI governance and digital transformation in hospitality firms and develops a sector-specific governance architecture. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 principles using Scopus as the sole database, resulting in a final corpus of 162 peer-reviewed articles published through August 2026. The selected literature was examined through bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny, alongside qualitative thematic synthesis to identify major research patterns and emerging governance concerns. Findings indicate rapidly expanding scholarly attention to AI-enabled hospitality, increasingly connecting artificial intelligence and digital transformation with sustainability, governance, smart tourism, and organisational decision-making. Thematic synthesis identifies five core areas: AI and algorithmic governance, data governance and cybersecurity, strategic governance of digital transformation, ethical and responsible AI, and fintech and decentralised governance. Building on these findings and established governance perspectives, the study proposes the ADAPT-H Framework, comprising seven interconnected pillars: Accountability, Data Stewardship, Algorithmic Transparency, People-Centred Governance, Technology–Strategy Alignment, Regulatory Harmonisation, and Ecosystem and Vendor Governance. The framework addresses hospitality-specific challenges and supports responsible, transparent, and strategically aligned AI adoption.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Governance, Sales Growth, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Tax Avoidance
summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the effect of corporate governance, proxied by institutional ownership and independent commissioners, sales growth, and firm size on tax avoidance in manufacturing companies in the consumer non-cyclicals subsector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from companies’ annual financial reports. The population consisted of 132 companies, while the research sample comprised 32 companies selected using purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria. The data were analyzed using EViews 12 to examine the effects of the independent variables on tax avoidance, both partially and simultaneously. The results indicate that corporate governance, sales growth, and firm size simultaneously have a significant effect on tax avoidance. Partially, corporate governance has a significant effect on tax avoidance, indicating that corporate governance mechanisms can influence companies’ policies in managing their tax obligations. Sales growth also has a significant effect on tax avoidance, suggesting that changes in sales growth may influence companies’ decisions regarding tax strategies. Meanwhile, firm size does not have a significant effect on tax avoidance. These findings are expected to contribute to companies, investors, and other stakeholders in understanding the factors that influence tax avoidance practices and in supporting more effective corporate governance and tax management.

title: From solo drivers to synergistic recipes: how smart manufacturing firms achieve high supply chain performance
summary: Driven by the global digital economy and industrial restructuring, smart manufacturing guides manufacturing-sector transformation, with supply chain management evolving into an integrated and dynamic collaborative model. However, technological, organisational, and environmental factors exert non-linear and interactive effects on supply chain performance. Drawing on the TOE framework, this study selects 50 A-share listed pilot smart manufacturing enterprises (2022–2023) as the sample, and combines fsQCA with multiple linear regression and interaction term models to explore the multi-factor configurations leading to high supply chain performance. The results show that the linear effects of individual antecedent conditions are limited and unstable; each condition's performance contribution can only be effectively realised within appropriate configurational contexts. Furthermore, four distinct pathways are identified: governance and resource synergy, structure and resource synergy, structure driven and multi-support, and supply chain driven. These findings provide practical path references for enterprises and support targeted policy formulation for government agencies.

title: Small firm, big shift: achieving results through digital transformation
summary: For small accounting firms, adopting artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled technology can help bridge skills gaps, improve productivity, and build competitive advantage. However, such investments involve risks and may not deliver expected results. This study examines the successful implementation of a new technology powered by AI in a small accounting firm, to automate functions of one of the services offered to clients. Using business process modelling and multiple factors, results from several viewpoints are presented. Findings show that the test user plays a crucial role by providing beneficial feedback during deployment, while resistance to change is the most significant challenge. Time savings, which generate monetary gains, and the allocation of skills to other value-added functions are the main goals pursued by managers. The primary benefit of the new technology is financial and covers cost reduction, and productivity, all of which contribute to the strategic benefit of developing a competitive advantage for the accounting firm.

title: Impact de la divulgation des informations ESG sur la création de la valeur actionnariale et la performance financière : cas des entreprises cotées à la Bourse de Casablanca
summary: Résumé L'importance croissante de la finance durable a accru l'attention portée aux pratiques de publication d'informations environnementales, sociales et de gouvernance (ESG), en particulier sur les marchés émergents. Au Maroc, les sociétés cotées sont de plus en plus encouragées à renforcer leur transparence et à intégrer des informations extra-financières dans leurs stratégies de communication, en réponse à l'évolution de la réglementation, aux attentes des parties prenantes et aux tendances en matière d'investissement durable. Cependant, les données empiriques concernant la relation entre la publication d'informations ESG, la création de valeur pour les actionnaires et la performance financière dans le contexte marocain restent limitées. Cette étude vise à examiner l’impact de la publication d’informations ESG sur la création de valeur pour les actionnaires et la performance financière des sociétés cotées marocaines. Plus précisément, elle cherche à déterminer si les entreprises qui présentant des niveaux de publication d’informations ESG plus élevés génèrent une plus grande valeur pour les actionnaires et obtiennent de meilleures performances financières. La recherche se concentre sur les entreprises non financières cotées à la Bourse de Casablanca sur la période 2020-2024. Cette étude adopte une approche quantitative fondée sur l’analyse de données de panel. Un indice de divulgation ESG sera élaboré à partir d’informations extraites des rapports annuels et des déclarations de développement durable. La création de valeur pour les actionnaires sera évaluée à l’aide du Q de Tobin, tandis que la performance financière sera mesurée à l’aide du ROA. Des variables de contrôle, notamment la taille, l’endettement et l’âge, seront également intégrées dans les modèles économétriques. L’analyse s’appuiera sur des régressions de panel à effets fixes, étayées par des tests de spécification de Hausman et des contrôles de robustesse. Les résultats trouvés ne donnent pas des preuves significatives de l’effet de la publication d’informations ESG sur la création de valeur pour les actionnaires ni sur la performance financière. Les résultats suggèrent également que la publication d’informations ESG des entreprises les plus jeunes renforce la confiance des investisseurs et contribue à la création de valeur à long terme au sein des sociétés cotées marocaines. Ces conclusions viennent étayer l’idée de plus en plus répandue selon laquelle des pratiques commerciales durables et transparentes constituent un moteur important de la compétitivité des entreprises et de leur viabilité financière sur les marchés émergents. Cette étude apporte une contribution à la littérature sur la finance durable et les pratiques ESG en fournissant des données empiriques issues du marché boursier marocain. Elle offre également des implications pratiques pour les dirigeants, les investisseurs et les régulateurs concernant l’importance stratégique de la publication d’informations ESG pour renforcer la valeur d’entreprise et la performance financière. Mots-clés : Publication d’informations ESG, création de valeur pour les actionnaires, performance financière, finance durable, sociétés cotées marocaines, données de panel. Abstract The growing importance of sustainable finance has increased the attention given to Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) disclosure practices, particularly in emerging and frontier markets. In Morocco, listed companies are increasingly encouraged to strengthen transparency and integrate extra-financial information into their communication strategies in response to regulatory developments, stakeholder expectations and sustainable investment trends. However, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between ESG disclosure, shareholder value creation and financial performance in the Moroccan context remains limited. This study aims to examine the impact of ESG disclosure on shareholder value creation and the financial performance of Moroccan publicly traded companies. More specifically, it seeks to determine whether companies with higher levels of ESG disclosure generate greater shareholder value and achieve better financial performance. The research focuses on non-financial companies listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange over the 2020–2024 period. This study adopts a quantitative approach based on panel data analysis. An ESG disclosure index will be developed using information extracted from annual reports and sustainability statements. Shareholder value creation will be assessed using Tobin’s Q, while financial performance will be measured using ROA. Control variables, including firm size, debt, and age, will also be incorporated into the econometric models. The analysis will rely on fixed-effects panel regressions, supported by Hausman specification tests and robustness checks. The findings do not provide significant evidence of the effect of ESG disclosure on shareholder value creation or financial performance. The results also suggest that ESG disclosures by younger companies strengthen investor confidence and contribute to long-term value creation among Moroccan listed companies. These findings support the increasingly widespread view that sustainable and transparent business practices are a key driver of corporate competitiveness and financial viability in emerging markets. This study contributes to the literature on sustainable finance and ESG practices by providing empirical data from the Moroccan stock market. It also offers practical implications for executives, investors, and regulators regarding the strategic importance of ESG disclosure in enhancing corporate value and financial performance. title: The Procurement Professional in the AI Era: Procurement Capability under Technological Change and Strategic Supply Uncertainty
summary: This independent professional research paper examines whether established procurement competency frameworks sufficiently articulate the capabilities required of practitioners operating in an environment shaped by artificial intelligence, changing international trade relationships and strategic supply uncertainty. Using a comparative analysis of the Government of Canada's Procurement Community Competencies and the United Kingdom's Government Commercial Function People Standards, the paper identifies areas in which existing professional standards may benefit from more explicit, observable and assessable behaviours. The research proposes a three-part capability architecture that retains established procurement competencies while introducing seven AI-related practice areas and four wider strategic practice areas. These address AI-supported decision-making, governance, evidence verification, trade and policy interpretation, supply-chain resilience, public-value trade-offs and integrated commercial judgement. An Ontario procurement-policy case study illustrates how these capabilities may be applied within a provincial environment. The paper also considers transferability across Canadian jurisdictions, recognising differences in legislation, trade obligations, policy requirements and institutional governance. A worked procurement decision exercise, proposed assessment criteria and an independent validation methodology provide a practical basis for professional discussion and future pilot testing. The proposed framework has not yet been empirically validated. Related publication This research builds upon the professional-development architecture explored in Rajbinder Kaur's book, The Procurement Professional: A Career Guide for the AI Era (2026). The book provides a structured learning pathway across procurement practice, commercial judgement, leadership, risk, resilience and digital transformation, while the research paper examines how those capabilities may be articulated and assessed in contemporary procurement environments. title: Does sustainable finance strengthen corporate governance? Evidence from ASEAN banks
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe growing global demand for the integration of strong corporate governance in the banking industry is essential for enhancing financial performance. However, the interactive role of sustainable finance in strengthening governance mechanisms remains relatively underexplored. This study aims to examine whether adopting sustainable finance practices strengthens corporate governance mechanisms in the banking sector in ASEAN countries during the period 2018–2022. Utilizing the Fixed Effects Model, this study presents a notable finding. The results indicate that the interaction between management scores and green bonds has a positive and significant effect on Return on Assets, whereby a 5% increase in green bonds exposure raises ROA by 0.248, but exerts a negative effect on Return on Equity, with a decrease of 0.340 for every 1% increase. In contrast, the interaction between shareholder scores and green bonds has a negative and significant impact on ROA, with a decline of 0.223 for each 5% increase, while positively influencing ROE by 0.222 for every 1% increase. This study confirms that green bonds asymmetrically moderate the relationship between corporate governance and banking performance, in which management-oriented governance enhances asset efficiency but suppresses ROE, whereas shareholder-oriented governance reduces ROA while improving ROE. Conceptually, green bonds function as a balancing mechanism between corporate governance and banking performance, whereby managerial governance improves asset efficiency at the expense of equity returns, while shareholder-based governance enhances ROE with the trade-off of lower ROA.

title: When Is ESG Performance Associated with Firm Value? The Moderating Role of Employee Turnover
summary: This study examines the relationships among ESG performance, employee turnover, and firm value and investigates whether employee turnover conditions the valuation relevance of ESG performance firms of different sizes across Taiwanese firms using data from 2019 to 2024. The study uses 10,247 firm-year observations to classify firms into smaller and larger firm-size groups using K-means clustering based solely on firm size and estimates the relationships across the full sample and the two size-based groups. The findings show that ESG and environmental performance are positively linked to firm value, especially in the larger firm-size group. Corporate governance performance is positively associated with firm value only in the larger firm-size group, while social performance shows no significant direct effect. Employee turnover is negatively associated with firm value in the larger firm-size group and conditions the ESG–firm value relationship. Moderation effects are significant among smaller firms, whereas the moderating effect of employee turnover on social performance is significant among larger firms. The study contributes to the ESG–firm value literature by incorporating employee turnover as a human-capital condition and by demonstrating a firm-size effect on ESG valuation. The findings suggest that ESG performance and workforce stability should be considered jointly when assessing the potential value implications of corporate sustainability practices.

title: Prevention, Law Enforcement, and Protection Strategies in the Digital Economy Ecosystem: An Integrated Legal Governance Framework for Indonesia
summary: Indonesia’s digital economy expands financial inclusion, market access, and transactional efficiency, but also increases exposure to fraud, phishing, identity theft, data breaches, ransomware, and payment abuse. This study examines the adequacy of Indonesia’s legal and institutional arrangements for preventing, investigating, and remedying economic cybercrime and formulates an integrated governance model. Using normative legal research, the study applies statutory, conceptual, comparative, and case approaches to legislation, regulatory instruments, institutional materials, and recent scholarship. The analysis finds that Indonesia possesses substantial criminal, data-protection, electronic-system, financial-sector, and consumer-protection rules, yet their operation remains fragmented across institutions and stages of response. Prevention still relies excessively on user awareness; enforcement is constrained by volatile evidence, uneven capacity, delayed asset freezing, and cross-border barriers; and remedies do not consistently restore victims’ finances, identities, or procedural position. The study proposes an Integrated Digital Economic Security Governance framework comprising a shared risk taxonomy, prevention by design, differentiated platform duties, coordinated evidence preservation and enforcement, victim-centred remedies, accountable international cooperation, and continuous evaluation. Its novelty lies in allocating responsibility according to institutional capacity, knowledge, and control while linking cybersecurity, law enforcement, corporate accountability, and victim recovery within one rights-based and risk-responsive legal architecture.

title: Toward Sustainable Supply Chains: The Spillover Effects of Customer Environmental Disclosure on Supplier Carbon Emissions
summary: Supply chain decarbonization is essential for achieving corporate sustainability and broader climate goals, yet emission reduction across organizational boundaries remains difficult because lead firms and suppliers often operate under fragmented environmental information. Although environmental information disclosure (EID) is increasingly viewed as an important instrument for improving corporate transparency, existing research has primarily examined its consequences within firm boundaries, leaving its cross-organizational sustainability implications insufficiently understood. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines whether customers’ environmental management disclosure is associated with upstream suppliers’ carbon emissions and conceptualizes the reduction of environmental information asymmetry as a key channel through which such disclosure may influence suppliers. Using a panel of 2213 supplier-year observations constructed from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2022, we estimate fixed-effects panel regressions to examine the relationship between customer environmental disclosure and supplier carbon intensity. The results show that suppliers exposed to environmental information disclosure from at least one customer have approximately 10.95% lower estimated carbon emissions, while a one-point increase in the average environmental disclosure score of a supplier’s customer base is associated with approximately 2.96% lower estimated supplier carbon emissions. Further analyses show that disclosure strength does not significantly moderate this relationship, whereas the characteristics of disclosed information matter: positive environmental disclosure strengthens the negative association between customer disclosure and supplier carbon intensity, while negative disclosure weakens it. These findings extend research on environmental disclosure beyond the focal firm by documenting its association with environmental outcomes across supply chain relationships. They also suggest that customer disclosure may transmit clearer environmental signals, thereby contributing to more sustainable and resilient supply chains.

title: Corporate Governance, Leverage, and Working Capital Turnover as Predictors of Financial Health in Indonesian Logistics and Transportation Companies
summary: Background: Financial vulnerability remains important in capital-intensive logistics and transportation companies during periods of disruption and recovery. Objective: This study examines the associations of leverage, Working Capital Turnover, and institutional ownership, used as a corporate governance proxy, with the financial health of Indonesian logistics and transportation companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Methods: A balanced panel of 75 firm-year observations from 15 companies during 2020–2024 was analyzed using Pooled OLS, Fixed Effects, and Random Effects estimators. Model selection was guided by the Chow, Breusch–Pagan Lagrange multiplier, and Hausman tests. Results: The Random Effects model was selected. Leverage was not significantly associated with the Altman Z-Score (β = 1.32, p = 0.294), so H1 was not supported. Working Capital Turnover had a significant negative association (β = −0.076, p = 0.021); because this direction contradicted the positive hypothesis and the ratio contained extreme values linked to negative working capital, H2 was not supported. Institutional ownership had the strongest significant positive association among the predictors in the selected model (β = 25.60, p < 0.001), supporting H3. Conclusion: Institutional ownership is positively associated with financial health, while the WCTO result requires cautious interpretation because of its denominator structure and overlap between the predictors and components of the Altman Z-Score.

title: Evolución de la responsabilidad social corporativa en las pymes (2002-2025). Análisis bibliométrico y revisión crítica de un campo en consolidación
summary: This article examines the evolution of corporate social responsibility (CSR) in SMEs between 2002 and 2025 through a bibliometric analysis and a critical review of 1,343 articles indexed in Web of Science and Scopus. The trajectory of the field is organized into four stages - initial, take-off, consolidation, and expansion - and traces the shift from ethical approaches, centered on the owner-manager, toward strategic perspectives linked to sustainability, innovation, legitimacy, and performance, reinforced in recent years by ESG frameworks and the circular economy. The field now appears mature and interdisciplinary, although longitudinal and sector-specific studies remain scarce. Its application to SMEs in the art market is proposed as a future line of research.

title: An audit-ready EHR foundation model for order-time medication-safety auditing across health systems
summary: Real-time medication-safety auditing requires current laboratory and medication histories, yet electronic health records (EHRs) may contain stale or missing decisive evidence. We present ClinicalGPT, an audit-ready foundation model using Clinical Trajectory Language to encode time, units, provenance, and observability, and workflow-aligned objectives to handle structured missingness. Across seven health systems, we retrospectively evaluated 847,000 eligible high-risk medication orders against a reference vector frozen before final scoring. The primary endpoint was the reference-standard-defined order-time failure-to-alert rate: eligible tier-i/ii reference-positive orders receiving no actionable alert at a system’s frozen operating point, per 1000 eligible orders. This offline process metric did not measure subsequent clinical actions, adverse drug events, or patient harm. ClinicalGPT with hard constraints achieved 3.2 misses per 1000 orders, versus 9.4 for rules only, 6.1 for the original generic LLM comparator, and 4.8 for the strongest observed LLM comparator (RAG + LLM + rules). Its false-alert rate was 33.9 (95% CI, 31.6–36.3), versus 38.7 for rules only. A separate single-site silent prospective assessment evaluated workflow measures without altering care. Matched ablations supported explicit observability modeling; independent de novo labeling of an enriched knowledge-base–independent subset preserved sensitivity ordering but narrowed the ClinicalGPT–RAG gap. These findings support comparative order-time auditing performance but do not establish clinical effectiveness or reduced patient harm.

title: From AI Readiness to Productivity: The Role of Innovation Capacity in Europe's Digital Transformation
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly expected to enhance productivity, yet technological adoption alone may be insufficient to generate measurable economic gains. This study examines how AI and digital readiness are associated with productivity across European economies and whether this relationship operates through innovation capacity and human capital. Using a balanced dataset covering the EU-27 in 2021, 2023, and 2024, we estimate a Partial Least Squares Path Modelling (PLS-PM) model linking AI/Digital Readiness, Innovation Capacity, Human Capital, Productivity, and Inclusive Growth, with country-cluster bootstrap inference. The results indicate an indirect-only mediation pattern: AI/Digital Readiness is strongly associated with Innovation Capacity but has no significant direct relationship with Productivity, whereas Innovation Capacity is strongly associated with Productivity and generates a significant indirect effect. Human Capital neither mediates nor moderates this relationship, and Productivity is not significantly associated with Inclusive Growth. The innovation-mediated pathway remains significant across several alternative specifications, although it becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero when business R&D expenditure is excluded from Innovation Capacity. Leave-one-country-out cross-validation also indicates substantial predictive relevance for Productivity. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between digital readiness and productivity in European economies is closely associated with the innovation capabilities through which technological opportunities can be translated into economic value.
