title: Corporate social responsibility as a strategic resource: examining the mediating role of corporate reputation in securing competitive advantage
summary: Introduction Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is increasingly described as a strategic intangible resource. Yet, the mechanism by which it converts into competitive advantage (CA) remains underspecified, and evidence from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies is limited. Drawing on stakeholder theory and the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines corporate reputation (CR) as the pathway that links CSR to CA in organizations operating in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Methods A cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Structured questionnaires were delivered to 200 managers using convenience sampling, with 150 valid responses retained. The measurement quality was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis, average variance extracted (AVE), composite reliability, and the Fornell–Larcker criterion. We addressed common method variance through procedural remedies and Harman’s single-factor test. Hypotheses were tested using ordinary least squares regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4, 5,000 resamples), controlling for firm age, organization size, and organization type. Results CSR was positively associated with CR ( B = 0.746, p < 0.001) and CR was positively associated with CA ( B = 0.403, p = 0.001). The total effect of CSR on CA was positive and significant ( B = 0.526, p < 0.001); however, the direct effect was not significant once CR entered the model ( B = 0.226, p = 0.061). The indirect effect through CR was significant [ B = 0.301, 95% bootstrap CI (0.079, 0.507)] and accounted for approximately 57.2% of the total effect, indicating an indirect-only (full) mediation. Discussion The results suggest that CSR relates to competitive advantage mainly through corporate reputation, rather than directly affecting competitive position. Reputation therefore appears to operate as the conversion mechanism that translates stakeholder approval into a resource position that is valuable, rare, and difficult to imitate.

title: Can large language models assess enterprise digital transformation?
summary: Enterprise digital transformation reshapes business models and operations through digital technologies, making scientific measurement essential for empirical research. This study proposes a large language model (LLM)-based multi-indicator and multi-level text measurement framework for identifying and classifying enterprise digital technology applications from two dimensions: digitalization and effectiveness. We further adopt a three-dimensional experimental design covering output modes, prompting strategies, and fine-tuning to evaluate model performance. The results show that LLMs generally outperform traditional machine learning (ML) models, even under Zero-shot settings. Synchronous multi-indicator output generally performs better than one-by-one output, whereas the effects of chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting and fine-tuning vary across models and tasks. Model performance varies across specific models and task settings, with both recent general-purpose models and reasoning-oriented models showing competitive results in different scenarios. Further analysis indicates that LLMs perform better on explicit digital technology indicators but show weaker performance on digital effectiveness indicators requiring contextual inference. Additional validation with non-Chinese multilingual LLMs and significance analysis supports the robustness of the main findings. This study provides a methodological tool and empirical evidence for measuring enterprise digital transformation using corporate disclosure texts.

title: Industry 4.0 and the premises for organizational decision-making: a multi-layer analysis
summary: Purpose The article approaches Industry 4.0 through the lens of social systems theory. It studies the impact of Industry 4.0 as a strategic initiative on organizational programs setting the premises for decision communication. Design/methodology/approach The study proceeds interpretively on seminal publications on Industry 4.0 and a collection of documents on application. Using hermeneutic analysis, it identifies criteria for correct decision-making on four layers of organization in society that are addressed in literature. Findings Different criteria are identified for the manufacturing sector as a whole, national industrial complexes, single companies and their systemic substructures. All of them are relatable to the idea of keeping the respective organizations in charge of the ongoing digital transformation by demonstrating innovativeness. Originality/value The study draws attention to the role of Industry 4.0 in communication constituting organization through decisions. It enables a discussion of strengths and weaknesses from a new perspective, giving a more nuanced account of Industry 4.0 as a strategic initiative.

title: Friend or Foe? The Role of Brand and CSR in the Animosity–Travel Relationship Under Boycott Contexts
summary: This study aims to extend research on the consumer animosity–travel relationship by examining consumer boycotts directed at global companies from a target foreign country. Additionally, we theorize the boundary conditions of product brand strength and the corporate social contributions of global companies to better predict the dynamic nature of the consumer animosity–travel relationship. Using two datasets collected from South Korean consumers (Study 1: 504 participants in 2020; Study 2: 478 participants in 2022), we employ Hayes’ PROCESS macro to test our moderated mediation hypotheses. The key findings are as follows. Corporate social contributions mitigate the positive indirect effect of consumer animosity toward economic sanctions on intentions to travel to a target country through increased boycott intentions. Contrary to our prediction, the brand strength of global products strengthens this same indirect effect. By integrating these findings across two independent studies conducted at different time points, this study offers important theoretical and practical implications. Specifically, the effects of brand strength and corporate social responsibility (CSR)—typically viewed as positive marketing signals in contemporary marketing philosophy—may differ substantially in the context of consumer boycotts during periods of international conflict.

summary: Аннотация. В статье рассматриваются изменения требований к кадровому потенциалу торговых предприятий в условиях цифровой трансформации. Анализируется влияние автоматизации, искусственного интеллекта, маркетплейсов и цифровых платформ на содержание трудовых функций и компетенции работников. Особое внимание уделяется формированию нового профиля цифровых компетенций, развитию механизмов up-skilling и re-skilling, а также внедрению современных форм цифрового обучения персонала. Обосновывается необходимость перехода от преимущественно внешнего найма к системному развитию кадров внутри организации. Предложен комплексный подход к управлению развитием персонала, включающий аудит цифровых компетенций, формирование матрицы навыков, непрерывное обучение и оценку его влияния на операционные показатели торгового предприятия. Ключевые слова: цифровая трансформация, торговые предприятия, кадровый потенциал, цифровые компетенции, искусственный интеллект, up-skilling, re-skilling, цифровое обучение, развитие персонала, автоматизация. Abstract. This article examines changing requirements for the workforce of retail enterprises amidst digital transformation. It analyzes the impact of automation, artificial intelligence, marketplaces, and digital platforms on job functions and employee competencies. Particular attention is paid to defining a new digital competency profile, developing upskilling and reskilling mechanisms, and implementing modern forms of digital staff training. The article substantiates the need to shift from a reliance on external hiring to the systematic development of personnel within the organization. A comprehensive approach to managing staff development is proposed, encompassing a digital competency audit, the creation of a skills matrix, continuous learning, and an assessment of its impact on the retail enterprise's operational performance. title: From reform to compliance: Unveiling the efficacy of green finance policy in curbing firm financial fraud
summary: As an institutional arrangement transitioning from blueprint to practice, green finance holds significant potential in shaping firm behavior; however, its mechanisms remain underexplored. Using a multi-period DID design and taking the establishment of the Pilot Zones for Green Finance Reform and Innovation as a quasi-natural experiment, this study explores the effect of the pilot policy on firm financial fraud. The results indicate that the pilot policy significantly reduces firm financial fraud, with the policy effect exhibiting a certain degree of lag. This finding remains valid after a series of robustness tests, including variable substitution, alternative model specification, and PSM-DID analysis. The pilot policy effectively targets the core elements of the fraud triangle, reducing the motive for firm financial fraud by lowering firm risk-taking and negative public sentiment pressure while also reducing the opportunity for fraud by alleviating information asymmetry. This study provides a reference for evaluating the effectiveness of green finance policies and offers insights into using institutional means to combat illegal firm activity.

title: Industrial Land Acquisition and Corporate Financing Preferences: Based on the Land Transaction Data From China
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the interplay between governmental land resource allocation and its micro‐firms and market efficiency implications within China's unique land system. Using data from A‐share companies listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen between 2007 and 2021, this study empirically examines how industrial land acquisition influences corporate capital structure decisions. The results indicate that post‐land acquisition, firms exhibit a significant debt financing preference, counter to China's conventional equity financing preference but congruent with the Pecking Order Theory. This behaviour shift is attributed to an informational effect, reducing the cost of debt capital while increasing the cost of equity capital due to perceived investment risk. However, firms receiving discounted land concessions achieve simultaneous reductions in both costs of debt and equity, suggesting capital markets prioritise government‐endorsed projects. The study concludes that applying the Modigliani‐Miller Theory in China requires incorporating institutional transaction costs embedded in the land allocation process.

title: Knowledge Management as An Innovation Strategy: Knowledge Management In The Context Of Manufacturing and Service Industry
summary: Knowledge management (KM) has become an important strategic tool for innovation, but the way it is applied and its effect is differential between manufacturing and service industries is not well understood. This paper provides an examination of KM as an innovation strategy through the lens of understanding how KM processes – creation, storage, sharing, application and transfer - drive innovation outcomes in manufacturing and service settings. The study draws on the knowledge-based view (KBV) and the SECI model to highlight some of the critical research gaps, such as the lack of comparative cross-industry studies, the underexplored intervening role of innovation between KM and organizational performance, and limited incorporation of digital era enablers like AI and Industry 4.0 technologies. The paper presents a systematic literature review and a comparative analysis which leads to the conclusion that the primary applications of KM are process innovation and operational innovation in manufacturing companies, while customer-centric and service innovation are the main applications of KM in service companies. These investments have become strategic in today's world as the KM software market is expected to grow to USD 74.22 billion by 2034 from USD 20.15 billion in 2024. The results not only advance the theory but also enable better guidance to organizations on how they can use KM as one of the competitive assets in the digital economy.

title: Analisis Lisensi Font Digital Perspektif Ekonomi Syariah
summary: The development of the digital economy has encouraged the trade of intellectual works, including digital fonts, through various marketplace platforms. Digital font licensing involves not only the transfer of digital files but also the granting of usage rights under specific terms and conditions. This study aims to analyze the practice of digital font licensing by Brand Hero Studio through the Font Kingdom platform from an Islamic economic perspective, particularly regarding transaction mechanisms, clarity of benefits and licensing terms, rights and obligations of the parties, and their relevance to the principles of ijarah contracts. This study employs a socio-legal research approach combining normative and empirical juridical methods with a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the founder of Brand Hero Studio, non-participant observation of the Font Kingdom platform, and document analysis of the User License Agreement (ULA) and relevant legal materials. The findings indicate that digital font licensing grants consumers usage rights according to the selected license type without automatically transferring copyright ownership. The scope of use and licensing fees are important in ensuring clarity of benefits and compensation. These practices have characteristics relevant to the concept of ijarah, although their assessment depends on the clarity of rights, obligations, licensing authority, and mutual agreement between the parties. No indication of riba was found in the payment mechanism, while potential gharar and zalim require further assessment based on licensing clarity and proportionality of sanctions.

title: Driving sustainable banking performance: the roles of digital transformation, FinTech adoption, and financial inclusion under regulatory environment moderation
summary: Purpose With sustainability becoming a global priority, financial institutions increasingly use FinTech to support sustainable performance within evolving regulatory environments. This study investigates how digital innovation, specifically FinTech Adoption and financial inclusion, is associated with firms' sustainable performance while examining the moderating role of the regulatory environment in shaping these relationships. It also offers insights into how regulatory frameworks can support the use of digital tools to promote a more sustainable financial future. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a survey methodology to collect data from bank employees in Saudi Arabia. From a total of 402 survey responses, 385 were considered valid and used for analysis. The proposed relationships were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The study revealed that digital transformation was significantly linked to sustainable performance, FinTech Adoption, and financial inclusion. Fintech Adoption was positively related to financial inclusion and sustainable performance. The moderation analysis showed that the regulatory environment strengthens the association between financial inclusion and sustainable performance. However, it does not significantly moderate the relationships between FinTech Adoption and sustainable performance or digital transformation and sustainable performance. Originality/value This study contributes a perspective by applying the Resource-Based View and Technological Innovation Systems frameworks to examine how internal capabilities and regulatory support are associated with sustainable performance. It also addresses a contextual gap by focusing on the Saudi banking sector under Vision 2030 reforms. The findings provide partial support for the moderating role of the regulatory environment, highlighting the complexity of regulatory influence.

title: Environmental proactivity relates to perceived sustainability performance through green innovation and resource efficiency in Vietnamese manufacturing
summary: Manufacturers in emerging economies face simultaneous pressure to reduce environmental impacts and preserve operating competitiveness, yet a proactive environmental orientation does not automatically translate into broad sustainability gains. Drawing on the natural-resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, and institutional theory, this study examines two internal conversion mechanisms green innovation capability and resource efficiency and the contextual role of perceived environmental institutional pressure. Survey data from 278 knowledgeable informants in Vietnamese manufacturing firms were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, bootstrap mediation and moderation tests, robustness analyses, and 10-fold cross-validation. The findings show that environmental proactivity is associated with perceived sustainability performance both directly and indirectly through two complementary routes: renewal through green innovation capability and operational optimization through resource efficiency. Institutional pressure is positively associated with green innovation capability, but it does not significantly amplify the proactivity–innovation relationship. The study contributes by specifying how strategic environmental intent is converted into sustainability-oriented capabilities rather than treating orientation as a self-executing resource. For managers and policymakers, the results support a balanced portfolio that combines innovation capability building with resource-efficiency improvement, while using external pressure together with technical support, implementation capacity, and green-finance access.

title: Future-ready Industrial systems: A RIDIT approach to evaluating industry 4.0 technological and strategical readiness of MSMEs
summary: Industry 4.0 (I4.0) adoption among micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in emerging and resource-constrained regions is shaped by heterogeneous technology adoption patterns and varying strategic priorities. The aim of this study is to empirically examines the adoption stages of selected I4.0 technologies and strategic dimensions among MSMEs in Jammu & Kashmir, India. A quantitative exploratory research design was employed using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire from 220 MSMEs. The seven I4.0 technologies that are used in this study are Big Data (BD), Digital Supply Chain (DSC), Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing (CC), Robotics, 3D Printing and Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV) and six strategic dimensions including Servitization, Supply Chain Integration (SCI), Machinery and Database Integration, Lean Manufacturing (LM), Green Manufacturing (GM) and Design-to-Cost were evaluated using a five-point Likert scale. RIDIT analysis was used to find the ordinal response distributions among the relative strategic priorities selected for this study. The findings reveal heterogeneous technology implementation with DSC recorded the highest quantity of completed implementation (15.24%), while CC showed the highest combined proportion of current and completed implementation (48.17%), followed by IoT (43.30%). AGV exhibited the highest consideration rate (56.10%) but the lowest completed implementation (6.71%). The strategic analysis indicates that GM received the highest mean RIDIT score (0.5863), followed by Design-to-Cost (0.5675) and Machinery and Database Integration (0.5031), whereas LM recorded the lowest relative preference (0.4256). The results reveal that the technological implementation and strategic priority dimensions do not follow the same trajectory due to the multifaceted dependability of the I4.0 transition. It provides empirical evidence from MSMEs in an understudied emerging market and illustrates the applicability of RIDIT as a reliable non-parametric prioritisation method. The results offer managers a framework for selecting I4.0 technologies and strategic dimensions that is supported by evidence. MSMEs should prioritise GM to improve operational efficiency and coordination before gradually investing in Servitization, system integration, design-to-cost, and LM.

title: Peningkatan Literasi Hukum Bisnis dalam Mewujudkan Kesejahteraan Era Digital bagi Perempuan di Kota Surakarta
summary: The Community Service Program (PKM) entitled “Enhancing Business Legal Literacy to Promote Digital-Era Welfare for Women in Surakarta City” aimed to improve women’s knowledge, awareness, and ability to understand and apply business law in entrepreneurial activities in the digital era. Information technology provides opportunities for women to develop businesses through social media, marketplaces, and various digital platforms, but it also creates legal challenges related to business legality, Business Identification Number (NIB), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), trademarks, business agreements, consumer protection, electronic transactions, and digital content use. The PKM activity was implemented through knowledge transfer, skills development, mentoring, and participant empowerment. The activities focused on understanding the rights and obligations of business actors, identifying legal risks, protecting products and trademarks, and using digital technology safely and responsibly. The program is expected to improve women’s business legal literacy, confidence, and ability to operate businesses legally, independently, creatively, innovatively, and sustainably. Improved legal literacy can help women prevent legal risks, protect their business interests, and optimize digital economic opportunities. Therefore, empowering women through business legal literacy can support entrepreneurial development and contribute to improving family and community welfare in Surakarta City. The program also emphasizes the importance of continuous learning and responsible digital practices to strengthen women’s capacity to face legal challenges and opportunities in the evolving digital economy.

title: TRANSFORMATION OF CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR MODELS UNDER MARTIAL LAW
summary: The transformation of consumer behaviour under martial law constitutes a relevant research problem in contemporary marketing theory. Economic instability, security risks, infrastructure and logistics disruptions, population mobility, digitalisation, and sustained psychological pressure significantly affect consumer needs, priorities, and purchasing decisions. Traditional determinants of choice, including price, quality, assortment, and accessibility, are increasingly supplemented by security, functional autonomy, supply reliability, reputational trust, and value congruence. The article addresses the theoretical and applied aspects of consumer behaviour in Ukraine under prolonged martial law, focusing on adaptation to a volatile socioeconomic environment. Consumer behaviour is considered as a dynamic system in which external changes influence the hierarchy of needs, resource allocation, information search, evaluation of alternatives, purchasing practices, and interaction with brands. Particular attention is devoted to the economic dimension of consumption. Financial constraints increase the importance of expenditure planning, price comparison, prioritisation of essential needs, and functional utility. At the same time, consumption may perform an emotional and compensatory function associated with maintaining habitual routines and psychological stability. The interaction between rational and emotional motives is therefore an important aspect of consumer behaviour under prolonged uncertainty. The article also considers security-related and functional characteristics of consumer value, including product availability, continuity of supply, reliability of delivery, and autonomous use. Digitalisation is examined in terms of expanding opportunities for searching, comparing, and verifying information, as well as reducing perceived purchasing risk. Attention is given to the value-based and reputational dimensions of consumer choice. Corporate social responsibility, ethical business practices, transparency, product origin, and public positioning may influence consumer attitudes towards brands under martial law. The article focuses on the interaction of economic, security-related, functional, digital, logistical, value-reputational, and emotional determinants of consumer behaviour. Their comprehensive consideration is relevant for developing theoretical approaches to behavioural patterns under prolonged instability and adapting marketing policies to a changing consumer environment.

title: Skill Constellations: Tracing the Supply Chain of Agent Skills on GitHub
summary: Agent skills are SKILL.md instructions and scripts that AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex run with the permissions of their user. Developers share skills by copying them between repositories, which makes them a software supply chain without a registry, versions or provenance. The origin of a copied skill, the reach of a security fix and the repositories that warrant review are therefore unknown. Studies that record which repositories hold a skill at a single point in time cannot reveal who copied it from whom. We contribute the first dated copy network of agent skills, built from the git history of every SKILL.md in GitSkills and covering 2,193,119 skill adoptions across GitHub, together with an interactive viewer. A few repositories are the source of almost all copies, and GitHub stars do not identify them. Skill copies almost never change with their source, and a fix at the source therefore rarely reaches them. We fit a model of which repositories others copy from and use it to rank repositories for audit. Reviewing the 100 repositories it ranks highest prevents 14.9% of later adoptions of high-risk skills, against 0.5% for the 100 most starred, which gives security engineers a short list to check before a skill spreads. Platforms should therefore distribute versioned references rather than copies. Project Website: https://fahdseddik.github.io/Skill-Constellations/

title: Environmental Responsibility in Saudi Banking: A Stakeholder Analysis of Green Finance Adoption
summary: ABSTRACT Green finance adoption in state‐directed emerging markets remains poorly understood among stakeholder groups. This study examines how environmental responsibility and green finance are interpreted, implemented, and governed in Saudi banking. Based on 25 semi‐structured interviews across nine stakeholder categories, reflexive thematic analysis identified five themes. Stakeholders agreed that banks' environmental responsibility extends beyond operations to capital allocation, but evaluated the credibility of green finance differently depending on institutional role. National policy was perceived to legitimise organisational attention more directly within banks than among SMEs. Weak measurement architecture emerged as a credibility‐risk pathway rather than evidence of intentional greenwashing. Organisational participants described resistance as mainly practical, although commercial tensions remained. Shari'ah governance was viewed as a conditional accountability resource when linked to technical verification and substantive oversight. The study offers a bounded, multi‐stakeholder explanation of green finance adoption. Regulators should strengthen proportionate market capacity; supervisors should test governance and evidential support; and standard setters should improve definitions, KPIs, comparability, and assurance.

title: Environmental Protection Tax and Corporate Green Innovation Persistence: Evidence from China
summary: Enhancing corporate green innovation persistence plays a vital role in shifting economic and social development toward greener, low-carbon models. This study treats the environmental protection tax (EPT) as an external institutional shock to the corporate green innovation system. Using data on Chinese A-share firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges from 2014 to 2023, this study uses a difference-in-differences (DID) approach to estimate the impact of the EPT on corporate green innovation persistence and explore its underlying mechanisms. Corporate green innovation persistence is measured by combining the dynamic change in firms’ green innovation output with the current scale of their green innovation activities. The findings show that the EPT significantly enhances corporate green innovation persistence. Mechanism tests further show that the EPT significantly reduces firm uncertainty, eases financing constraints, and increases R&D investment, providing evidence consistent with the proposed expectation-stabilization, resource-access, and resource-allocation mechanisms. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that the positive effect is more pronounced among firms facing lower industry competition, firms with greater institutional investor ownership, state-owned enterprises, firms with higher information transparency, non-high-tech firms, and firms whose executives exhibit a stronger risk-taking propensity. These results provide empirical evidence for strengthening the long-term innovation-guiding role of the EPT and offer policy insights into corporate sustainable development from a coordinated perspective of institutions, resources, and firm behavior.

title: Does Overvaluation Predict Earnings Management? Evidence on the Agency Costs of Overvalued Equity in a Frontier Market
summary: Most of the accounting literature on emerging markets asks whether capital markets reward high-quality earnings. This paper reverses the question and asks whether market valuation shapes subsequent reporting. Using 4981 firm-year observations for 619 non-financial Vietnamese listed firms, with misvaluation measured from 2016 to 2024 and earnings management from 2017 to 2025, and measuring misvaluation through the Rhodes-Kropf et al. decomposition alongside five Tobin’s Q-based measures, we find that overvaluation in one year predicts more aggressive earnings management in the next. The estimate is positive and significant at the one percent level for all six measures in specifications that absorb firm and year fixed effects, control for prior accrual behaviour, and use standard errors clustered by firm. A one within-firm standard deviation increase in the firm-specific error raises absolute discretionary accruals by 6.6 percent of their within-firm standard deviation. The accruals are directional, and the relation runs through magnitude rather than incidence: overvaluation predicts how large income-increasing accruals are once reported, but neither the probability that they are reported nor the probability of falling in the upper tail of the accrual distribution. The relation weakens as leverage rises, which is consistent with creditor monitoring; formal interaction tests do not support the corresponding predictions based on firm size or state ownership. A firm-block bootstrap that reproduces both first-stage models raises the standard error by 23 percent but leaves the confidence interval clear of zero, and randomisation inference across 1999 permutations places the estimate well outside the placebo distribution. The evidence is substantially stronger for within-firm variation than for cross-firm comparison: in a propensity-score matched sample the estimate is not distinguishable from zero and covariate balance is unsatisfactory. The design is observational and does not identify a causal effect. Because equity-based compensation and an active market for corporate control are largely absent in this setting, the findings indicate that the association does not depend on the channels through which price pressure is conventionally assumed to operate, although they do not identify the channel that does operate.

title: Pemetaan Bibliometrik Penelitian Literasi Pajak dan Kepatuhan Wajib Pajak pada Era Digital
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memetakan perkembangan publikasi ilmiah mengenai literasi pajak dan kepatuhan wajib pajak pada era digital. Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan bibliometrik untuk mengidentifikasi tren publikasi, artikel berpengaruh, pola sitasi, serta keterhubungan kata kunci dalam topik literasi pajak, kepatuhan wajib pajak, dan perubahan lingkungan perpajakan berbasis digital. Data penelitian diperoleh melalui Publish or Perish dengan menggabungkan tujuh file CSV yang kemudian dibersihkan, dibatasi pada periode 2016-2024, dan dianalisis menggunakan Microsoft Excel serta VOSviewer. Hasil pengolahan data menunjukkan bahwa publikasi terkait literasi pajak dan kepatuhan wajib pajak mengalami peningkatan, terutama pada 2022-2024. Visualisasi VOSviewer menunjukkan bahwa kata kunci tax literacy dan individual taxpayer compliance menjadi pusat jaringan, sedangkan kata kunci understanding, revenue, tax policy, tax law, digital economy, SMEs, dan business membentuk tema pendukung. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa penelitian mengenai kepatuhan wajib pajak pada era digital tidak hanya berkaitan dengan sistem administrasi pajak elektronik, tetapi juga dengan pemahaman pajak, kebijakan perpajakan, hukum pajak, penerimaan negara, dan aktivitas usaha dalam ekonomi digital. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi dalam menyajikan peta pengetahuan, celah penelitian, serta arah riset lanjutan mengenai literasi pajak dan kepatuhan wajib pajak pada era digital.

title: Government Reporting: Accounting Changes and Errors
summary: This study investigates factors associated with the recognition of accounting changes, adjustments, and accounting errors reported in accordance with GASB guidance. These data are used to determine what accounting changes, estimates and error corrections are reported in annual financial reports, and whether they support a basis for the GASB to issue Statement No. 100 amending GASB Statement No. 62 to improve financial reporting consistency, comparability and transparency. This study adds to the literature by examining the implementation and reporting of GASB accounting guidance on accounting errors and corrections, along with determinants identified in previous research regarding the impact on financial reporting of states, counties, and municipalities that warrant an amendment to recognition.

title: Navigating the Digital Frontier: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Accounting and Financial Reporting in Adamawa State, Nigeria
summary: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is precipitating a paradigm shift in global accounting and financial reporting practices. However, its adoption and impact in developing economies, particularly at the sub-national level, remain underexplored. This study investigates the impact of AI on accounting efficiency, financial reporting quality, and the operational dynamics of accounting firms in Adamawa State, Nigeria. Anchored on the Technology Organization Environment (TOE) framework, the study synthesizes existing literature to conceptualize the dual impact of AI, as a catalyst for automated reporting and fraud detection, and as a challenge concerning infrastructural deficits and skill gaps. The study proposes that while AI significantly enhances the timeliness and accuracy of financial reports in Adamawa State, its optimal adoption is severely constrained by erratic power supply, inadequate digital infrastructure, and a deficit in AI-relevant competencies among practitioners. The paper concludes that AI’s impact in Adamawa State is currently at a nascent but transformative stage, requiring deliberate policy and educational interventions. Recommendations include the integration of AI modules into the curriculum of tertiary institutions in Adamawa State, public-private partnerships for infrastructural development, and phased AI adoption strategies by accounting firms.

title: The Effects of Internal Corporate Social Responsibility Practices on Employee Job Satisfaction: Evidence From Commercial Banks in Zambia
summary: This study investigated the effects of internal Corporate Social Responsibility (iCSR) practices on employee job satisfaction among commercial banks in Lusaka, Zambia. The research examined two key dimensions of iCSR: education & training, and pay & benefits. The investigation was motivated by the need to understand how specific iCSR practices influence employee satisfaction in the Zambian banking context, where limited empirical research has been conducted despite the growing importance of human capital management in competitive banking environments. The study employed a descriptive research design utilizing a quantitative research approach. The study was grounded in the positivist research paradigm. Data was collected from 146 employees across 15 commercial banks operating in Lusaka through digital self-administered structured questionnaires, representing a 71.2% response rate from the target sample of 205 respondents. Stratified sampling technique was employed to ensure representative selection across management levels (senior, middle, and lower management). Data analysis was conducted using SPSS Version 29.0, employing descriptive statistics (frequencies, means, standard deviations), Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. Statistical significance was determined at p < 0.05 level. The study revealed exceptionally strong positive relationships between pay & benefits and education & training iCSR dimensions and job satisfaction. Pay and Benefits had a variance of (r = 0.9271, 85.96%. Education and Training demonstrated strong effects (r = 0.8935, 79.84% variance. A conceptual framework was developed that successfully integrated the two iCRS dimensions and their relationship with job satisfaction

title: The Impact of Crisis Magnitude in the Context of Corporate Ability and Corporate Social Responsibility Crises: The Roles of Expectancy Violations and Emotions
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates how the effects of crisis magnitude on individuals’ expectancy violations (EV) and emotions vary depending on the crisis type, specifically highlighting corporate ability (CA) crises versus corporate social responsibility (CSR) crises. We conducted a 2 (crisis magnitude: high vs. low) × 2 (crisis type: CA vs. CSR) randomised experiment with 269 participants in Hong Kong and mainland China. The results showed that in the case of CSR crises, crises with greater magnitude triggered stronger anger, disappointment, and regret than crises with lower magnitude through negative EV; however, such effects were not found in CA crises. In turn, these three emotions exerted different effects on attitudes and behavioural intentions. These findings offer insights into the underlying mechanisms of individuals’ cognitive and emotional responses to different crises and are expected to help crisis communicators develop effective strategies suitable for different types of crises.

title: Making sense of mixed signals: the impact of (In)consistent performance feedback on corporate digital technology innovation
summary: Abstract Digital technology innovation (DTI) is a vital source of competitive advantage in the digital transformation era. Drawing on the behavioral theory of the firm (BTOF) and the attention-based view (ABV), this study examines how consistent and inconsistent performance feedback influence firms’ digital technology innovation and how CEO attentional vigilance moderates these effects. Using data from Chinese A-share listed companies, we distinguish between mitigation and adaptation DTI to capture the heterogeneity of firms’ behavioral responses. The results show that when primary performance falls below aspiration, firms increase mitigation digital technology innovation but reduce adaptation digital technology innovation. In contrast, when feedback is inconsistent (primary performance below and secondary performance above aspiration), firms decrease mitigation (and increase adaptation) digital technology innovation. CEO attention quantity weakens (strengthens) the positive (negative) relationship between below-aspiration feedback and mitigation (adaptation) innovation, while CEO attention stability weakens (strengthens) the negative (positive) relationship between inconsistent feedback and mitigation (adaptation) innovation. These findings demonstrate how performance ambiguity and executive attention jointly shape the direction of DTI, advancing understanding of managerial cognition and organizational strategy in the digital context.

title: STRATEGIC FIT IN EMERGING MARKET SUPPLY CHAIN DESIGN: EVIDENCE FROM DANGOTE CEMENT PLC, NIGERIA
summary: Strategic fit requires a firm's supply-chain capabilities to support its competitive priorities and the characteristics of the environment in which it operates. However, conventional applications of strategic-fit theory can understate the influence of institutional and infrastructural conditions on supply-chain architecture in emerging markets. This review article examines Dangote Cement Plc in Nigeria as a single documentary case, integrating Porter's competitive-strategy perspective with Chopra and Meindl's strategic-fit framework. Corporate disclosures, established supply-chain literature and institutional evidence are analysed across facilities, sourcing, transportation, energy, inventory and information-related decisions. The analysis finds that Dangote Cement's documented configuration reflects extensive control over strategically important stages of the value chain, including limestone extraction, cement production, selected energy inputs and a substantial distribution capability. These choices support cost control, supply assurance, scale and market reach and can therefore be interpreted as mutually reinforcing elements of competitive and supply-chain strategy. The analysis further argues that foreign-exchange exposure and infrastructure unreliability should be treated as first-order supply-chain design variables in emerging-market contexts. Where imported inputs create currency exposure, electricity supply is unreliable or third-party logistics capacity imposes service uncertainty, the economic boundary between outsourcing and internalisation changes. Vertical integration, local sourcing, alternative fuels, captive logistics capability and redundancy may consequently represent strategic responses to environmental uncertainty rather than simple preferences for asset ownership. The study extends strategic-fit reasoning by proposing that emerging-market supply-chain design must align competitive priorities, demand characteristics and environmental constraints simultaneously. It recommends that firms evaluate network configuration using total risk-adjusted supply cost rather than purchase price alone.

title: Government Accounting Reform and Public Accountability: A Systematic Review of Themes, Methods, and Institutional Conditions
summary: Government accounting reforms promise more transparent, comparable, and decision-useful public financial information, yet evidence on their governance effects remains fragmented. This systematic literature review synthesizes 137 studies on IPSAS, accrual accounting, financial reporting, auditing, and related public-sector reforms. Following PRISMA 2020, records were identified across five scholarly sources, screened against predefined criteria, quality-appraised, and analyzed through descriptive mapping and thematic synthesis. Four recurrent themes emerge: IPSAS and accrual adoption; institutional implementation and decoupling; financial reporting and accountability; and auditing, internal control, and governance. The evidence shows that formal adoption does not automatically produce substantive implementation or stronger accountability. Outcomes depend on political commitment, administrative capacity, professional competence, audit quality, information usability, and the fit between imported standards and domestic institutions. Accrual reforms can improve information quality and governance, but they can also relocate discretion into estimates, valuations, and reporting choices. The review therefore develops a conditional reform-realization framework in which standards create potential value, organizational and institutional mechanisms convert that potential into practice, and accountability actors determine whether information becomes consequential. The study contributes a reconciled research map, identifies methodological weaknesses, and proposes a future agenda centered on longitudinal, causal, user-oriented, and sustainability-focused research.

title: Stay Ahead of Geopolitical Supply Chain Risks
summary: The conventional playbook for managing supply chain risk -- designed for natural disasters, supplier failures, and short term market volatility -- is falling short in the face of persistent, politically motivated disruptions such as trade wars, sanctions, and armed conflict. As the maneuverings of national leaders threaten supply chains, global companies are struggling to mount effective responses. At the heart of the challenge are high levels of both complexity and uncertainty. Long-standing US trade policies have been disrupted and become more unpredictable; acts of war or terrorism can upend executives' assumptions about security risk overnight. The scale and complexity of companies' supply chains make it challenging to predict the impact of such events across their net works. Against this backdrop, it's critical that companies make a more systematic effort to understand, monitor, and manage geopolitical risks.

title: Marketing Strategies of Enterprises' International Development in a Digital Environment: A Literature Review Based on Cross-Cultural Social Media Communication
summary: Digital transformation has reshaped firms' international marketing practices, with social media emerging as a vital communication channel for global brand outreach, yet cross‑cultural frictions often weaken marketing effectiveness. This paper adopts the literature review method. By sorting out studies collected from mainstream academic databases, it explores digital international marketing, cross‑cultural social media communication and corresponding corporate strategies. It first analyzes how digital platforms and big data analytics remodel traditional ways to enter foreign markets, pushing firms to focus more on long‑term brand relationship building. Drawing on cross‑cultural dimension theories, this work discusses how cultural differences exert moderating impacts on marketing performance, and explores the balance between global standardization and localized operation. It further investigates creator collaboration and interactive two‑way social media tactics, with special focus on resource‑constrained small and medium‑sized enterprises. This literature review also highlights the value of combining digital capabilities with culture‑responsive marketing practices during overseas expansion. Such integration enables firms to lift audience engagement, strengthen brand trust and adapt marketing plans to diverse consumer contexts. Finally, this review identifies research limitations including scarce cross‑national comparative evidence and insufficient studies on long‑term brand reputation. It also offers suggestions for future empirical exploration.

title: ESG Rating Divergence and Corporate Financial Resilience Under the Dual Carbon Goal: A Signal Noise Perspective from China
summary: In the turbulent volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity (VUCA) era, financial resilience is a critical strategic asset for energy, mining, and infrastructure (EMI) companies seeking to withstand external shocks and support sustainable development under the dual carbon goal. Although environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance is often viewed as a safety buffer, the growing divergence in observed ESG ratings may reduce the clarity of sustainability signals in capital markets, consistent with the signal-noise perspective. Drawing on signaling theory and information-asymmetry perspective, this study examines Chinese A-share EMI companies from 2015 to 2023 to investigate the impact of ESG rating divergence on firm-level financial resilience. Using a composite financial resilience index, a two-way fixed-effects model, and supplementary instrumental-variable and robustness checks, we find that ESG rating divergence is significantly and negatively associated with financial resilience. The mediation analysis provides evidence consistent with two potential transmission channels: tighter financing constraints and reduced analyst attention. Furthermore, the negative association is stronger among firms with lower information disclosure transparency, firms located in the eastern region, and firms audited by Big Four accounting firms. This study extends research on the economic consequences of ESG rating divergence and provides empirical evidence relevant to strengthening corporate financial resilience and long-term sustainable development under China’s dual carbon goal.

title: Urban Vernacular Transitions: Contesting Commercial Space Through Everyday Practices in Bangkok’s Privately-Owned Public Spaces
summary: This paper explores the transition of vernacular architecture from rural traditions to urban adaptations,expanding the discussion toward what may be termed the “urban vernacular.” While rural vernacular has longbeen associated with natural materials, collective labour, and the continuity of cultural wisdom, the urbanvernacular emerges in contexts marked by industrialised construction, consumer culture, and the negotiationof everyday life in rapidly growing cities. Privately-Owned Public Spaces (POPS) in Bangkok are introducedas illustrative cases through which these dynamics can be observed. Although designed as commercial interiors,malls and their semi-public areas are tactically re-appropriated by diverse groups: students transform foodcourts into study zones, elderly visitors establish routines of repeated occupation, and youth communitiesadapt mirrored walls for dance practice. Such activities reveal how POPS, despite their regulated and privatelymanaged frameworks, provide informal third places that foster social interaction, comfort, and adaptability. Thestudy employed non-participant observation and photographic documentation across selected malls, focusingon patterns of use that extend beyond consumption. These observations highlight how POPS serve as a lensto interpret broader processes of vernacular transition. The paper argues that urban vernacular heritage liesless in the preservation of form than in the recognition of lived practices that sustain cultural meaning. Byframing POPS as an example rather than an endpoint, the research underscores the resilience of improvisation,collectivity, and cultural continuity within contemporary urban conditions. While these spaces demonstratevernacular resilience through everyday improvisation, the analysis also exposes their precarity, a conditionshaped by surveillance, selective tolerance, and corporate governance that renders user autonomy contingentand unstable. This tension between resilience and precarity defines the contested terrain of urban vernacularpractices within Bangkok’s privately-owned public spaces.

title: Information and Communication Technology Penetration and Performance of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in East Africa: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) penetration has become an important enabler of Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) performance, competitiveness, innovation, and growth. However, empirical evidence on the relationship between ICT penetration and SME performance in East Africa remains fragmented across countries, technologies, sectors, and methodological approaches. This study systematically reviews empirical evidence on ICT penetration and SME performance in East Africa to synthesise existing findings, identify adoption barriers, and establish research gaps. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2015 and 2026 were identified, screened, and assessed using predefined eligibility criteria, resulting in 15 studies included in the final synthesis. The findings indicate that ICT penetration enhances SME performance through improved operational efficiency, market access, customer engagement, innovation, financial inclusion, business growth, and competitiveness. However, these benefits are constrained by limited digital skills, high technology adoption costs, inadequate ICT infrastructure, financial constraints, cybersecurity concerns, weak organisational readiness, and limited institutional support. The review further reveals that existing research is predominantly cross-sectional and country-specific, with limited comparative evidence across East Africa. Significant gaps remain concerning emerging technologies, rural and informal SMEs, long-term sustainability outcomes, and the mechanisms through which digital capabilities influence SME performance. The study concludes that sustainable digital transformation requires not only access to ICT but also affordable infrastructure, digital skills, organisational capabilities, and supportive institutional ecosystems

title: Financial Technology, Digital Transformation and Higher Education Outcomes: Evidence from Saudi Arabia in Comparative Perspective (2019–2023)
summary: Using comparative data for Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States over 2019–2023, this study examines conditional associations between Financial Technology (FinTech), digital infrastructure, and higher-education outcomes. The empirical unit is the country-year, yielding 25 observations (5 countries × 5 years). The empirical strategy combines descriptive cross-national benchmarking with parsimonious two-way fixed-effects panel models. The baseline models use the FinTech Penetration Index (FPI) internet penetration, Gross Domestic Product GDP per capita, and public education spending, with country and year fixed effects. The estimates show mixed conditional associations across enrollment, graduation, and administrative cost per student and are interpreted cautiously because only five countries are observed. Financial inclusion is treated as a theoretical mechanism that is not directly measured in the present panel. The study therefore provides a transparent comparative Financial Educational Technology (FinEdTech) framework while emphasizing the limits of inference from a small national panel.

title: From appraisal to adaptation: a dual-path model of construction project management professionals' job crafting in response to emerging smart technologies
summary: Purpose Emerging smart technologies (EST) – such as building information modeling, big data, cloud computing and robotics – have profoundly reshaped workflows and workplace behaviors in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Although extensive research has investigated the multi-level driving factors of EST implementation, little is known about its downstream effects on construction project management professionals' psychological and behavioral responses. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the transactional model of stress and self-determination theory, this study develops a “stress appraisal–psychological state–behavior response” theoretical model and empirically tests it using 315 construction project management professional samples. Findings The findings show that challenge appraisal of EST implementation is positively associated with role breadth self-efficacy, whereas hindrance appraisal is positively related to ego depletion. Furthermore, role breadth self-efficacy and ego depletion are found to mediate the relationships between challenge appraisal and hindrance appraisal and the three forms of job crafting, respectively. Moreover, conscientiousness strengthens the relationship between hindrance appraisal of EST implementation and ego depletion, while its moderating effect on the link between challenge appraisal and role breadth self-efficacy is not supported. Originality/value These findings contribute to the body of knowledge on individual-level psychological and behavioral adaptation to EST implementation in construction management. These findings offer valuable insights for managers to maximize the benefits of EST in projects by recognizing its double-sword role and driving the AEC industry's continued digital transformation.

title: Green absorptive capacity and environmental sustainability: unveiling the interplay and moderating roles of blockchain and supply chain finance
summary: Purpose Drawing on dynamic capability theory and the natural resource-based view, this study aims to examine how green absorptive capacity (GAC) enhances environmental sustainability performance (ESP) through financial performance (FP) and operational performance (OP) and how blockchain technology (BCT) and supply chain finance (SCF) strengthen these indirect relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 522 organisations in Egypt and 508 in Jordan. Covariance-based structural equation modelling was used to test the moderated mediation model. Findings The results show that in both Egypt and Jordan, GAC improves ESP indirectly through FP and OP. In Jordan, blockchain technology strengthens the indirect relationship through both financial and operational performance, whereas in Egypt these blockchain effects are not supported. Supply chain finance strengthens the indirect relationship through operational performance in both countries, but not through financial performance. The nested model comparison indicates that whilst the overall model applies to both contexts, BCT and SCF exert varying degrees of influence in Egypt and Jordan. Research limitations/implications The results can support policymakers and organisational stakeholders by showing how digital technologies and green financing mechanisms can be used to strengthen the impact of green knowledge on performance and accelerate progress towards environmental sustainability. Originality/value This study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation framework explaining how green absorptive capacity enhances environmental sustainability performance through financial and operational performance and how blockchain technology and supply chain finance strengthen these indirect relationships. By comparing Egypt and Jordan, the study extends dynamic capability theory and the natural resource-based view through context-specific evidence from two Arab emerging economies and reveals country-specific differences in the effectiveness of digital and financial enablers.

title: Omnichannel Bot Communication, Brand Awareness, and Purchase Intention: A Descriptive S-O-R Analysis in the GraPARI KBP Service Context
summary: Digital transformation has increased the demand for fast, accessible, and personalized service communication, making omnichannel bot communication increasingly relevant to telecommunications customer service. This study aimed to describe response patterns related to omnichannel bot communication, brand awareness, and purchase intention among Telkomsel customers in the Kota Baru Parahyangan (KBP) service context and to organize these findings using the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. A cross-sectional descriptive quantitative survey was conducted in March 2026 using Google Forms distributed through WhatsApp. Respondents included Telkomsel customers who visited GraPARI KBP and customers from the surrounding KBP community. Non-probability recruitment resulted in 133 complete responses. Thirteen researcher-developed items were analyzed at the individual-item level using frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations. The findings showed that personalization had the largest observed mean among the stimulus items (M = 4.73), while ease of access recorded a lower mean (M = 3.20). Brand recall showed a highly concentrated response pattern (M = 4.96). Purchase-intention responses were less uniform, particularly for preferential/consideration intention (M = 3.11), while exploratory intention showed no response variation. The study provides context-specific empirical evidence by using S-O-R as a conceptual framework for organizing descriptive findings rather than testing causal relationships. The findings highlight the relevance of personalization and service communication while also emphasizing the need for validated multi-item measures and inferential research to examine relationships among the S-O-R domains.

title: Benchmarking the digital paradox: performance measurement in outcome-based contracts
summary: Purpose Outcome-based contracts (OBCs) are emerging business models that can enhance returns from investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation. This study identifies the barriers to OBC adoption to explain how organizations can overcome the digital paradox – the under-realization of value from digital technology investments. Design/methodology/approach The study integrates the Grey Systems Theory with the DEMATEL (Grey-DEMATEL) to address uncertainty in expert judgments and to identify, rank and analyse the causal interrelationships among barriers to OBC adoption. Findings The results show that digitally-enabled OBCs (eOBCs) represent an incomplete contracting phenomenon, with barriers spanning technology, strategy, governance and performance measurement. The study identifies joint ownership as a critical mechanism for overcoming these barriers by facilitating asset evolution, improving performance measurability, reducing monitoring costs and safeguarding legitimacy and competencies. It further demonstrates that ownership should be viewed as dynamic, with ex post ownership determined by the party whose investments best sustain long-term value creation. Research limitations/implications The study advances understanding of the digital paradox by integrating transaction cost economics, generalized property rights theory and digital servitisation. Future research could examine industry contexts, investment risks and cross-country differences in digital asset formation. Practical implications The findings underscore the importance of collaborative technology provider–user relationships, continuous value chain reconfiguration and adaptive ownership allocation to maximize value from digital technology investments. Originality/value This study provides a novel theoretical framework explaining how digitally transformed OBCs can unlock business value from digital technologies and mitigate the digital paradox.

title: Online Teaching and Learning in South Asian Higher Education: Challenges and Emerging Opportunities for Teacher Education and Physical Education
summary: Abstract Online teaching and learning has become a permanent component of higher education, yet its educational value depends on more than access to digital platforms. This critical integrative review examines the development of online higher education in South Asia and focuses specifically on its implications for teacher education and physical education. Drawing on recent regional reports, peer-reviewed reviews, policy documents and foundational theories of online learning, the review synthesises evidence concerning digital inequality, faculty competence, learner engagement, assessment, academic integrity, artificial intelligence, accessibility and quality assurance. The analysis shows that South Asian institutions have moved from pandemic-era emergency remote teaching toward a more complex phase of sustainable digital transformation, but progress remains uneven across countries and institutions. Teacher education requires explicit development of digital pedagogical competence, authentic assessment and supervised professional practice, while physical education requires a discipline-sensitive blended model because embodied, psychomotor and safety-related outcomes cannot be fully reproduced online. Generative AI offers emerging opportunities for personalised learning, feedback, multilingual support and professional development, but it also introduces risks related to privacy, bias, academic integrity and over-reliance. The review proposes a Context-Responsive Online Teaching and Learning Framework built around infrastructure readiness, pedagogical alignment, faculty competence, learner support, inclusive access, authentic assessment, discipline-sensitive design and responsible innovation. The article argues that the future of online higher education in South Asia should not be defined by the quantity of technology adopted, but by the quality, equity and educational purpose with which technology is integrated. title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN AND INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an important technology for transforming modern supply chain and inventory management. Supply chains today face challenges such as uncertain demand, inventory shortages, excess stock, transportation delays, rising costs and changing customer expectations. AI helps organizations address these challenges by using technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, Internet of Things (IoT), computer vision, robotics and intelligent automation. AI can analyse large volumes of historical and real-time data to improve demand forecasting, inventory planning, procurement, warehouse operations and transportation management. In inventory management, AI helps organizations maintain optimum stock levels, reduce stock-outs, identify slow-moving products and automate replenishment decisions. AI also supports supplier evaluation, risk identification and real-time monitoring of supply chain activities. The application of AI can improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, increase accuracy and enhance customer satisfaction. However, organizations may face challenges such as high implementation costs, data quality issues, cybersecurity risks, lack of skilled employees and difficulties in integrating AI with existing systems. Effective implementation therefore requires reliable data, suitable infrastructure, employee training and appropriate human oversight. The integration of AI with IoT, cloud computing, robotics and advanced analytics is expected to further improve supply chain visibility and responsiveness. Thus, Artificial Intelligence is becoming a valuable tool for creating efficient, flexible and data-driven supply chain and inventory management systems.

title: The Role of Work-Life Balance and Safety & Health as Internal Corporate Social Responsibility Practices in Enhancing Job Satisfaction: Evidence from Commercial Banks in Lusaka, Zambia
summary: This paper aims to examine the effects of Internal Corporate Social Responsibility (iCSR) practices on employees' job satisfaction, with specific focus on work-life balance and safety and health within commercial banks in Lusaka. In this paper, it is also aimed to explore the relative role of these iCSR dimensions in shaping job satisfaction in a developing country context where empirical evidence remains limited. We employed a quantitative research design using structured questionnaires administered to employees across 15 commercial banks. A dataset of 205 employees was collected, of which 146 valid responses were analyzed. Data were analyzed using SPSS Version 29, applying descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis. Main findings of the study demonstrate that (i) work–life balance has a strong and statistically significant positive effect on job satisfaction (r = 0.9268, p < 0.001), accounting for 85.9% of the variance and emerging as the most significant predictor; (ii) safety and health shows a positive correlation (r = 0.926), but is not a statistically significant predictor in multivariate analysis, suggesting it functions as a hygiene factor; and finally (iii) iCSR practices can be differentiated into motivational and baseline factors, contributing to theoretical understanding while providing a Sub-Saharan African perspective. The study offers practical implications, indicating that banks should prioritize work-life balance initiatives while maintaining safety and health standards. It also provides guiding knowledge for policymakers and managers seeking to enhance workplace satisfaction and improve iCSR implementation.

title: Analysis of Factors Influencing Digital Transformation Readiness in Hospitals Using the Organizational Digital Transformation Readiness and TOE Framework
summary: Digital transformation readiness in healthcare extends beyond the availability of technology to the organizational and environmental conditions that shape the implementation of digital solutions in practice. This study aimed to identify and analyze digital transformation readiness components, refine them based on contextual empirical evidence, organize them through the integration of Organizational Digital Transformation Readiness (ODTR) and Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE), and assess stakeholder consensus using the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM). A qualitative-dominant sequential design was employed in a single specialized eye hospital involving nine purposively selected participants with domain relevant expertise. Interview data were analyzed using a framework-guided hybrid deductive inductive thematic analysis. The same nine participants subsequently completed the FDM phase; accordingly, FDM was used to assess within-panel stakeholder consensus and refine the candidate components rather than as independent external validation. The analysis produced 23 readiness components, all of which met the predefined FDM consensus criteria and were organized across the Technology (5), Organization (14), and Environment (4) domains. Three context-derived refinements, EM01 Specialty-Specific Features, EM02 Service Continuity, and EM03 Vendor Dependency, were incorporated into the corresponding TOE domains without forming an additional domain. In the context of the specialized eye hospital studied, the findings indicate that digital transformation readiness involves the interrelationship between technological resources and processes, organizational capabilities and governance, human and cultural readiness, and the external digital health environment. The resulting contextual framework provides a traceable structure for understanding and reviewing digital transformation readiness within the organizational setting examined and may support context-sensitive planning for hospital digital transformation.

title: Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure and Firm Performance: Evidence from Saudi Listed Firms
summary: The objective of this research is to find out if supply chain sustainability disclosure is related to firm performance among publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia. A unique and valid Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure Index (SCDI) that has six variables is measured based on the standards in the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) (2019) which are GRI 204, GRI 308, and GRI 414 through a systematic content analysis of 142 annual accounts of 58 publicly-listed non-financial corporations on the Saudi stock exchange (Tadawul) from 2022 to 2025

title: Atlantica Cinemas Limited: Behind the Screens at a Small Business Audit
summary: ABSTRACT This CPA‐style case focuses on Atlantica Cinemas, an independent cinema chain operating in Atlantic Canada. Students are called upon to draft an audit planning memo that considers the nature of the company's operations, structure, and ownership. Several key financial reporting issues are also explored. This case is designed for capstone or early graduate‐level courses, as well as later portions of undergraduate audit and assurance courses where students have experience with financial reporting and assurance topics.

title: Does the kind of sustainability disclosure change its market value? A theory-elaborating meta-analysis of disclosure form and capital-market valuation
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis asking whether the kind of sustainability-related disclosure explains heterogeneity in its association with market-based firm valuation. Much of the literature treats ESG disclosure, sustainability reporting, integrated reporting and the separate environmental, social and governance disclosures as interchangeable indicators of one construct. This review treats that functional-equivalence assumption as testable. Using information-based disclosure theory, it specifies disclosure kind on four theoretical dimensions, namely information granularity, reporting architecture, external assurance and standards alignment, and tests whether splitting the construct improves the explanation of the accumulated evidence on market valuation. Registered before the main search.

title: The Impacts of Deglobalisation on Global Supply Chains and China's Policy Responses
summary: For decades, economic globalisation has given rise to a highly specialised and cost-efficient global supply chain system. Nevertheless, in recent years, overlapping trade protectionism, public health crises and geopolitical games have fuelled the wave of deglobalisation, severely threatening the stability of global industrial and supply chains. This paper first reviews the evolution of globalisation and the existing literature to clarify its research focus, and analyses the underlying causes of deglobalisation from three dimensions: political factors, sudden external shocks and internal economic drivers. It further discusses profound transformations triggered by deglobalisation from three perspectives: spatial layout of supply chains, operational costs and risks, and differentiated impacts on China. Based on China's national reality, this paper systematically sorts out China's targeted countermeasures in four aspects: independent and controllable domestic industrial chains, coordinated regional industrial chains under RCEP, diversified market layout via the Belt and Road Initiative, and the construction of an early warning system for supply chain risks. Finally, it summarises the whole paper and predicts the future evolution of global supply chains, offering references for China's long-term stable participation in international division of labour.
