title: EFEKTIVITAS LAYANAN KENAIKAN PANGKAT PADA BADAN KEPEGAWAIAN DAN PENGEMBANGAN SUMBER DAYA MANUSIA KABUPATEN GOWA
summary: Civil servant promotion services represent a strategic apparatus career development instrument directly affecting work motivation, performance recognition, and civil apparatus welfare. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of promotion services at the Personnel and Human Resources Development Agency (BKPSDM) of Gowa Regency amidst the digital transformation of civil service administration. A qualitative approach with a descriptive method was employed, involving eight key informants selected through purposive sampling techniques. Data collection was carried out through semi-structured interviews, passive participant observations, and administrative document reviews from February to April 2026. Data analysis followed the interactive model encompassing data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing based on Steers' three dimensions of organizational effectiveness: goal attainment, integration, and adaptation. The results reveal that promotion services at BKPSDM Gowa Regency have generally operated effectively through the implementation of the State Civil Apparatus Information System (SIASN), inter-agency coordination with the National Civil Service Agency (BKN) and regional apparatus organizations (OPD), and adaptation to recent promotion periodization regulations. However, service effectiveness remains sub-optimal due to administrative discrepancies, delayed document revisions from proposing agencies, and periodic system maintenance bottlenecks. ABSTRAK Layanan kenaikan pangkat merupakan instrumen strategis pembinaan karier Aparatur Sipil Negara (ASN) yang berdampak langsung pada motivasi kerja, pengakuan kinerja, dan kesejahteraan aparatur. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis efektivitas layanan kenaikan pangkat pada Badan Kepegawaian dan Pengembangan Sumber Daya Manusia (BKPSDM) Kabupaten Gowa di tengah transformasi digital layanan kepegawaian. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode deskriptif yang melibatkan delapan informan kunci yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi partisipatif pasif, dan telaah dokumen administratif selama periode Februari hingga April 2026. Analisis data dilakukan melalui model interaktif yang mencakup reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan berdasarkan tiga dimensi efektivitas organisasi Steers, yaitu pencapaian tujuan (goal attainment), integrasi (integration), dan adaptasi (adaptation). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa layanan kenaikan pangkat pada BKPSDM Kabupaten Gowa secara umum telah berjalan efektif melalui implementasi Sistem Informasi Aparatur Sipil Negara (SIASN), koordinasi lintas sektor bersama Badan Kepegawaian Negara (BKN) dan Organisasi Perangkat Daerah (OPD), serta adaptasi terhadap regulasi periodisasi kenaikan pangkat terbaru. Namun demikian, efektivitas layanan belum sepenuhnya optimal akibat kendala ketidaksesuaian data administratif, keterlambatan perbaikan berkas dari instansi pengusul, dan hambatan teknis koneksi sistem (maintenance).

title: The impact of governance on strengthening audit practices and promoting financial transparency: an empirical investigation in the Iraqi business context
summary: This study examines the relationship between corporate governance mechanisms and financial disclosure among companies listed on the Iraq Stock Exchange. Drawing on agency theory and stakeholder theory, the study considers how internal and external governance arrangements influence transparency in an emerging market characterized by institutional and regulatory constraints. The study employs a quantitative research design based on firm-year data from 19 listed companies over the period 2018–2022, yielding 95 observations. Financial disclosure is measured using a structured disclosure index derived from annual reports. The governance variables include board structure, managerial ownership, ownership concentration, audit committee presence, remuneration committee presence, risk committee presence, and the external auditor’s opinion. The findings indicate that governance mechanisms linked to active monitoring, particularly audit and risk committees, are positively associated with financial disclosure. Remuneration committees and unqualified audit opinions also show positive relationships with disclosure, while ownership concentration is negatively associated with transparency. Board structure does not show a statistically significant effect, suggesting that formal board arrangements alone may not be sufficient to enhance disclosure in this context. The study contributes to the governance and disclosure literature by providing empirical evidence from the Iraqi business environment, where institutional constraints may shape the practical effectiveness of governance mechanisms. The results offer implications for regulators, policymakers, and boards seeking to strengthen financial reporting practices and improve investor confidence in emerging markets.

title: The Influence of Fraud Star on Financial Report Fraud with Audit Quality as a Moderating Variable (Empirical Study of Manufacturing Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the Period 2021 – 2024)
summary: Financial statement fraud can undermine the credibility of accounting information and harm stakeholders. This study aims to analyze the association between Fraud Star elements and financial statement fraud, with audit quality as a moderating variable. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data from financial statements and annual reports of basic materials manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024. Purposive sampling resulted in 41 companies with 164 observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with IBM SPSS Statistics 29. The results indicate that financial targets have a significant positive association with financial statement fraud, whereas nature of industry and rationalization have significant negative associations. Capability and lack of integrity show no significant associations. Regarding moderation, audit quality strengthens the relationship between financial targets and financial statement fraud, while weakening the relationships involving nature of industry and rationalization. However, audit quality does not moderate the relationships involving capability and lack of integrity. These findings provide insights into the relationships between Fraud Star elements, audit quality, and financial statement fraud.

title: International Trade Policies and Sustainable Environmental Governance in Nigeria: A Legal Appraisal
summary: The intensification of global trade has increasingly positioned international trade law as a key instrument of environmental governance, extending its traditional commercial function to promote sustainability. This article critically examines the legal impact of international trade policies on sustainable environmental governance in Nigeria, whose economy remains heavily dependent on crude oil exports and other primary commodities. Adopting a doctrinal and comparative legal methodology, this evaluation assesses Nigeria's constitutional, statutory, and institutional frameworks in conjunction with multilateral trade agreements, regional trade instruments, and international environmental treaties, drawing comparative insights from the United Kingdom, the United States, and South Africa. The article argues that although Nigeria possesses an extensive legal and institutional framework for environmentally sustainable trade, its effectiveness is undermined by the non-justiciability of environmental obligations under Chapter II of the Constitution, weak regulatory enforcement, institutional fragmentation, and dependence on environmentally intensive exports. It further contends that legal scholarship has largely treated trade liberalisation and environmental protection as separate fields, overlooking the dual role of international trade law in both facilitating and constraining domestic environmental governance. Through doctrinal analysis of legislation, case law, and treaty provisions, supported by comparative institutional evaluation, the article demonstrates that Nigeria's principal challenge lies not in the absence of legal norms but in deficiencies in implementation and enforcement. It recommends constitutional recognition of enforceable environmental rights, integration of sustainability standards into trade and investment legislation, and strengthened regulatory institutions to align Nigeria's trade regime with evolving global environmental governance and sustainability requirements.

title: Digital Transformation of Political Parties in Russia: Organisational Activities and Legal Restrictions
summary: Introduction. Digital technologies are transforming not only the methods of political communication but also the organisational and procedural forms of activity carried out by the political parties. Expansion of remote electronic voting practices, implementation of digital form of signature collection, electronic preliminary voting, as well as creation of party platforms and services based on the artificial intelligence technologies emphasize the relevance of the issues of transparency of digital procedures, personal data protection, cybersecurity, and equality of political participation. The scientific problem set forth in the study refers to the existing model of legal regulation of political party status in Russia, which is mainly based on the territorial and organisational principle and, therefore, creates non-conformity of the party institution juridical construct to the actually developing digital forms of its activity. The aim of the study is to reveal the main trends in digital transformation of political parties in Russia, assess legal and organisational consequences of this process, and propose approaches to improving legal regulation of party activities. Materials and Methods. The study is based on the analysis of the laws regulating political party activities, elections, and personal data protection, as well as empirical data on digital activity of political parties. Dogmatic legal, system analysis, historical and content analysis methods were used to conduct the study, as well as legal modeling approach to developing a risk-based regulatory model. Results. It has been established that digital transformation of the parties evolves at three interconnected levels: procedural, organisational, and communication-political. It has been shown that digitalization not only expands the scope of the forms of participation for party supporters having no formal membership, and transfers certain party functions to e-platforms, but also causes new risks arising from the verifiability of digital procedures, automated data selection and processing, and creation of synthetic content. Having a single set of requirements for all digital activities has been proved to be insufficient: the scope of guarantees should depend on the legal significance of a procedure and potential consequences of a technical error. Discussion and Conclusion. Based on the results of the study, a risk-based approach to regulation of digital activities of a political party has been proposed. The scope of legal guarantees should depend on the scope of potential consequences of using digital procedures, and ensure the availability of accessible offline alternative, transparency of automated processing, independent audit, and efficient monitoring and appeal mechanisms. The theoretical significance of the study lies in differentiation of the levels of political party digital transformation, whereas practical significance – in the possibility of using the proposed model for improving the legislation and internal party regulation.

title: HowArtificial Intelligence Will Pay Your Subsistence
summary: This essay examines the proposition articulated in the source video essay Como a Inteligência Artificial Vai Pagar Sua Subsistência (How Artificial Intelligence Will Pay Your Subsistence), which argues that artificial intelligence may soon enable a largely autonomous economic production system whose dividends could replace labor income as the material basis of household subsistence. Treating the video as its primary object of analysis, the essay reconstructs its argument into eight propositions and evaluates them in relation to the economics of automation, post-work political theory, and the political economy of distribution. Three research questions organize the inquiry: (1) under what technological and institutional conditions could production become sufficiently autonomous to approximate the system described in the video; (2) why, and through which institutional mechanisms, would the owners of autonomous capital have incentives to share its surplus with the broader population; and (3) what would happen to bargaining power, individual freedom, and social stability during a transition in which automation advances faster than redistribution. The analysis produces four principal findings. First, the vision of autonomous production is economically and technologically coherent in principle, but it is highly contingent in practice. It should therefore be understood not as an inevitable consequence of technological progress, but as an institutional configuration shaped by ownership structures, property rights, taxation, corporate governance, and political decisions. Second, the redistribution anticipated by the video has a recognizable functional logic. If automation substantially reduces the role of labor while production capacity continues to expand, maintaining aggregate demand may require mechanisms capable of distributing purchasing power beyond conventional wage employment. However, historical and comparative evidence suggests that the decisive mechanism is more likely to be public policy than voluntary corporate benevolence. Third, the most consequential risks are political rather than purely technological. A society in which productive capital becomes increasingly autonomous could weaken labor's traditional sources of bargaining power, including the ability to withdraw labor, change employers, or negotiate collectively. It could also create forms of income that are conditional, programmable, politically revocable, or dependent on centralized technological infrastructures. The transition itself may represent the greatest danger, particularly if mass automation occurs years or decades before effective redistribution institutions are established. Fourth, the central question is not whether artificial intelligence can generate abundance, but how the ownership and distribution of that abundance are constitutionally and politically organized. The same technological capacity could contribute either to unprecedented material freedom or to unprecedented economic dependence. Autonomous machines do not determine the political structure of the society in which they operate. Ownership, institutional checks and balances, democratic accountability, and the legal status of the social dividend determine whether automation becomes a mechanism of emancipation or a new architecture of dependency. The essay concludes by proposing institutional design principles for a post-labor transition, emphasizing broad participation in productive capital, predictable and legally protected distribution mechanisms, limits on discretionary control over basic income, democratic oversight of highly autonomous productive systems, and institutional safeguards against excessive concentration of economic and political power. Under these conditions, artificial intelligence could contribute not merely to the substitution of human labor, but to a transition toward a society in which technological productivity expands the material conditions of human autonomy rather than diminishing them.

title: The Influence of Mobile Money and FinTech Apps on Consumer Spending Habits in Nigeria
summary: As digital financial services rapidly expand across emerging markets, understanding the determinants of mobile money usage is critical for deepening economic inclusion. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this study investigates the impact of Perceived Convenience, Perceived Security, and Perceived Usefulness on the Consumer Spending Habits of FinTech users. A positivist, cross-sectional research design was employed, using purposive sampling to survey 294 semi-literate female traders across three major open-air markets in Obio Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria. Data were validated and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that Perceived Convenience is the strongest positive driver of consumer spending habits, followed by a moderate positive influence from Perceived Usefulness. Notably, while Perceived Security established robust internal reliability, it exerted the weakest direct effect on transaction volume, suggesting that it functions as a baseline expectation rather than an active catalyst for usage. The study concludes that while secure infrastructure is necessary to establish initial trust, frictionless user experiences and tangible daily utility are the primary engines of sustained digital financial engagement. Consequently, FinTech developers and policymakers are advised to prioritise seamless ecosystem integrations tailored to middle-aged demographics to accelerate digital economy participation.

title: From Human Judgment to Machine Learning: A Philosophical Study of Knowledge Creation in Modern Accounting
summary: Background: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning into accounting and auditing has transformed the creation, validation, and application of professional knowledge, raising questions about the legitimacy of algorithmic knowledge in accounting practice. Objective: This study examines the epistemological shift from human judgment to algorithmic knowledge in the implementation of Financial Accounting Standards (Standar Akuntansi Keuangan [SAK]) and Quality Management Systems (Sistem Manajemen Mutu [SMM]). Methods: This study employs a qualitative-interpretive approach through conceptual analysis and an examination of practitioners’ perspectives on the reliability, transparency, explainability, and trustworthiness of AI-assisted decision-making. Results: The results of the study show that AI can improve efficiency, predictive accuracy, and analytical capabilities in modern accounting practices but, at the same time, poses epistemological challenges in the form of limited algorithmic transparency, limited explainability, and the potential erosion of auditors’ professional skepticism. Although the conceptual analysis indicates that AI can positively affect efficiency and predictive accuracy, it also raises epistemic challenges related to transparency, accountability, and the preservation of professional skepticism. The shift from judgment-based knowledge to data-driven inferential knowledge has transformed the traditional epistemic authority held by accountants and auditors. The application of SAK and SMM in the accounting profession has implications for defining professional responsibilities in maintaining the quality of financial reporting and audit processes. Conclusion: This study proposes a human–machine epistemic partnership, in which AI functions as an analytical augmentation tool while accountants and auditors remain the primary epistemic authorities.

title: Making Shrimp in Moral Economies: Time, Ethics, and Labor in a Global Supply Chain
summary: ABSTRACT This article is part of the special issue 'Morality at Work: Ethnographies of Labor and Ethics' edited by Michael Vine and Sarah Winkler‐Reid. This article explores how future‐oriented temporalities shape people's labor experiences and ethical subjectivities within the global supply chain of brown shrimp. Drawing on ethnographic research with Dutch fishers, Moroccan shrimp peelers, and European processing managers, it traces how embedded notions of risk, luck, and destiny mediate workers' engagement with the uncertainty of the future. Processing company managers in Europe employ risk management practices to assert control over volatile markets, while North Sea fishers rely on notions of luck to navigate the unpredictability of fishing. In Moroccan peeling factories, workers often invoke destiny when making sense of their precarious working conditions. This article argues that attention to these divergent orientations toward the future offers critical insight into the moral economies that drive different forms of work under global capitalism.

title: Digital Transformation Disclosure and Green Technological Innovation Toward Sustainable Manufacturing: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Green technological innovation is important to the sustainable development of manufacturing. As a core driver of transition toward sustainable production patterns, green innovation helps firms reduce environmental externalities while maintaining economic competitiveness. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and the Knowledge-Based View, this study examines the association between digital-transformation disclosure and green technological innovation using 16,231 firm-year observations for Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2015 to 2022. Green technological innovation is measured by green patent applications, and the baseline specifications use negative binomial models with year and industry fixed effects, province-clustered standard errors, and a full control set that includes firm size. Digital-transformation disclosure is positively associated with green patent applications. Parallel-mediation estimates and province-clustered Bootstrap confidence intervals identify significant indirect effects through inter-organizational knowledge flow, R&D expenditure intensity, and the R&D personnel share. In terms of point estimates, the R&D personnel indirect effect is the largest of the three, followed by knowledge flow and R&D expenditure; however, only the R&D personnel versus R&D expenditure difference is statistically significant, and the three channels are better characterized as complementary. The difference between the knowledge-flow and R&D-expenditure effects is marginally significant. The hypothesized inverted-U moderating pattern of market competition is not statistically significant in the preferred specification with industry and year fixed effects. Split-sample estimates show directional heterogeneity across region, ownership, and firm size, but formal interaction tests do not reject equality of the digital transformation disclosure coefficients across groups. These results document robust associations rather than definitive causal effects and highlight the complementary roles of knowledge recombination, R&D expenditure, and technical personnel in green patenting. These findings carry implications for sustainability-oriented research and management practice by documenting channels through which digital-transformation disclosure is associated with green patent activity in the manufacturing sector.

title: Regenerative gastronomic tourism and short food supply chains: a SOR model approach
summary: Sustainable food systems depend not only on how food is produced but also on how consumers form trust, identity, and lasting relationships with local producers. Regenerative gastronomic tourism, rooted in ancestral knowledge and place-based culinary practices, has emerged as a catalyst for short food supply chains (SFSCs), yet the psychological mechanisms converting immersive culinary experiences into sustained demand remain poorly understood. This scoping review synthesizes evidence published between 2016 and 2026 through the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework, integrating consumption value and social identity perspectives. Regenerative experiences, heritage workshops, farm visits, and digital stimuli activate internal consumer states, including perceived authenticity, territorial identity, groundedness, and multidimensional consumption value. These states drive willingness to pay price premiums, post-trip purchasing, and digital advocacy, with tourist-generated word-of-mouth feeding back as stimuli for future consumers. The discussion identifies critical gaps: longitudinal loyalty decay, digital mediation after the trip, community sovereignty risks, contextual diversity, and greenwashing resistance. The SOR framework offers a conceptual pathway to inform the potential scaling of regenerative gastronomic tourism as an economic lever for sustainable food system transformation.

title: The Transparency‐Capability Dilemma: Configuring Stakeholder‐Engagement to Overcome Scope‐3 Inertia in Net‐Zero Supply Chains
summary: ABSTRACT Scope‐3 decarbonisation is central to a credible net‐zero strategy. However, firms face a difficult transparency‐capability dilemma. They are under immense pressure to disclose supply chain emissions, while the collaborative capabilities needed to act are slow‐building, relational, and unevenly distributed across supplier systems. This paper explains how firms can configure stakeholder engagement so that Scope‐3 transparency supports collaborative decarbonisation rather than becoming a source of unmanaged exposure. Drawing on a structured conceptual review and interpretive synthesis, we develop a stakeholder engagement architecture comprising carbon‐intelligence sourcing, collaborative carbon co‐design, and carbon‐governance commons. It theorises these as interdependent engagement configurations, explaining how supplier emission information becomes decision‐useful carbon intelligence, how such intelligence supports collaborative implementation with suppliers, and how repeated collaboration can be stabilised through accountable governance. The paper develops propositions, diagnostic configurations, and boundary conditions explaining why Scope‐3 engagement may become substantively coupled, weakly coupled, or symbolically claimed.

title: The Mediating Role of Green Supply Chain Management between Lean Manufacturing Practices and Sustainable Performance
summary: The Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA)-registered multinational manufacturing companies in Laguna continue to face financial, social, and sustainability challenges despite adopting Lean Manufacturing Practices (LMP). However, evidence remains limited on how Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) enhances the sustainability outcomes of lean initiatives in the Philippine manufacturing context. This study examined GSCM's mediating role in the relationship between LMP and Sustainable Performance (SP) among PEZA-registered multinational manufacturing companies in Laguna. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, data were collected from middle- to upper-level managers through a researcher-made questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, regression analysis, and mediation analysis. The findings revealed that selected LMP dimensions significantly influenced SP, while GSCM significantly mediated the effects of selected LMP on financial, social and environmental performance. The results indicate that environmentally responsible supply chain practices can serve as an important pathway linking selected lean manufacturing practices with sustainable performance. Based on these findings, the study proposed a strategic plan to help PEZA promote sustainable manufacturing practices and enhance the competitiveness of multinational manufacturing companies. The study provides empirical evidence that integrating lean and green practices is essential to achieving long-term sustainable performance and advancing the Philippines’ goal of becoming a leading sustainable manufacturing hub in Asia.

title: Renewable Energy Output Uncertainty and Risk Transmission in Sustainable Power Supply Chains
summary: Uncertainty in renewable energy output changes how risk is allocated among generators and electricity retailers. We develop a mean–variance model with a thermal plant, a green plant, and a retailer under retailer-led Stackelberg and generation-side Cournot arrangements. In the Stackelberg arrangement, greater retailer risk aversion raises the purchase price and both outputs by compressing the retailer’s unit-margin exposure. In the Cournot arrangement, greater thermal-plant risk aversion lowers thermal and total output but raises green output, the expected purchase price, and renewable share. At the baseline endpoints, green share falls from 55.9% to 51.6% in the former arrangement and rises from 54.8% to 74.1% in the latter. The green plant’s optimal mean output is independent of its own risk coefficient under additive zero-skewness, quadratic-profit, and decision-independent uncertainty conditions; a skewed-shock counterexample shows where this shielding can fail. Local, global, and distributional sensitivity checks and 5000 feasible parameter draws reproduce the analytical directions while showing that magnitudes are calibration dependent. Because renewable share can move opposite to absolute renewable generation, sustainability assessment should report generation levels, shares, procurement prices, and risk allocation together. The model does not estimate emissions, welfare, or reliability.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Digitalization on Competitive Advantage at Maersk company in Saudi Arabia
summary: This study examines the impact of supply chain digitalization on competitive advantage at Maersk in Saudi Arabia. Digitalization is operationalized through internal functional integration supported by enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and interorganizational information sharing supported by Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity. A descriptive-analytical approach was adopted, using a structured questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale. Responses from 66 employees were suitable for analysis. Cronbach’s alpha for the 20-item instrument was 0.933, indicating high internal consistency. Both digitalization dimensions were rated very highly: ERP-supported integration had a mean of 4.38 and an average item standard deviation of 0.67, while IoT-supported information sharing had a mean of 4.26 and an average item standard deviation of 0.77. Competitive advantage had an overall mean of 4.24. Indicators of internal operational capabilities, including continuous improvement and responsiveness, ranked above ultimate outcomes such as market share and entry into new markets. Response dispersion showed a systematic pattern: internal integration items exhibited less variation than items concerning information exchange with external partners, suggesting more consistent willingness to cooperate than execution of cooperation. Simple linear regression identified a strong, positive, statistically significant relationship between digitalization and competitive advantage (R = 0.757; R² = 0.574; F(1,64) = 86.128; reported p < 0.001). Digitalization thus explained approximately 57.4% of the variance in competitive advantage. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities perspective, the study argues that returns on digital investment depend on organizational routines built around technology. Recommendations address system integration, partner segmentation by digital maturity, data governance, and workforce development. Measurement and research-design limitations constrain generalizability and causal interpretation.

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Transformation on Innovation Performance in Manufacturing Enterprises
summary: This study investigates the impact of digital transformation on the innovation performance of listed manufacturing companies and explores the mediating mechanism of R&D expenditure. Utilizing a sample of Chinese firms, the empirical results demonstrate that digital transformation exerts a significantly positive impact on innovation efficiency and performance, with R&D expenditure serving as a critical bridging mechanism. This study enriches the existing theoretical framework, offering empirical evidence for digital strategies while suggesting future inquiries into firm heterogeneity.

title: ESG performance, board gender diversity and corporate financial performance: the role of countries’ cultural orientation in European companies
summary: Purpose This paper aims to investigate the relationship between environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance and corporate financial performance (CFP), focusing on the moderating role of board gender diversity and the influence of national cultural orientation. Design/methodology/approach This study performs a fixed effects linear regression analysis with time effects on a panel data set of 889 European listed companies (5,004 firm-year observations) across 17 industries and 22 countries over the period 2016–2023. Findings The results of this study reveal that ESG performance reduces CFP. However, the presence of women sitting on the board positively moderates the above relationship. Also, the results show that the moderating role played by board gender diversity in the relationship between ESG performance and CFP varies according to the cultural orientation of the firm’s country of headquarters. Research limitations/implications This study focuses on the short-term financial effects of ESG performance and only includes European-listed companies with available data. It does not account for other board characteristics and uses the GLOBE project for cultural classification, which may not capture all institutional dimensions. Practical implications The findings of this study suggest that increasing board gender diversity can enhance the financial benefits of ESG performance, especially in countries with lower gender egalitarianism. This study also highlights the need for context-sensitive governance and sustainability strategies that align with national cultural characteristics. Originality/value This paper contributes to the literature by jointly examining internal (board gender diversity) and external (national culture) moderating factors in the ESG–financial performance relationship.

title: Development of an Artificial Intelligence Maturity Framework for Organizational Governance and Digital Transformation
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven digital transformation has become a strategic priority for organizations seeking to enhance competitiveness, operational efficiency, and innovation. However, existing AI maturity models primarily emphasize technological capabilities or data readiness, with limited integration of AI governance, risk management, ethics, organizational capabilities, and digital transformation into a comprehensive framework. This study aims to develop an Artificial Intelligence Maturity Framework to assess AI implementation maturity and support organizational digital transformation planning. The research employs a Framework Development Study approach by integrating Systematic Literature Review (SLR), Comparative Framework Analysis, Content Analysis, and Design Science Research (DSR). The framework is synthesized from existing AI maturity models, ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the OECD AI Principles, and recent studies on AI Governance and Responsible AI. The proposed Integrated AI Maturity Framework comprises a conceptual model, a matrix of dimensions and indicators, five maturity levels, a conceptual assessment instrument, and an AI implementation roadmap. The framework integrates nine dimensions: strategy, AI governance, AI risk management, AI ethics, data, technology, organizational capabilities and talent, innovation culture, and digital transformation. It provides a comprehensive conceptual foundation for evaluating and advancing sustainable AI implementation across diverse organizational contexts.

title: A systematic benchmarking pipeline for demand forecasting and inventory-aware supply chain decision support
summary: Demand forecasting has been shown to be one of the key facilitators of successful supply chain and inventory management. In this work, we introduce a benchmarking pipeline for demand forecasting in retail that includes data preprocessing, comparative benchmarking of different machine learning/deep learning (ML/DL) approaches, and decision-focused evaluation. Unlike other works that compare predictive performance of ML/DL models and end there, our pipeline links reproducible ML/DL benchmarking and decision-focused evaluation through cost of inventory management in order to derive costs from forecasting error/bias. We also present a scalability study on another retail dataset. Several standard forecasting models, such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), CNN-LSTM, and XGBoost, are compared using a unified experimental pipeline on benchmark retail datasets. The experimental results reveal that while the deep learning models efficiently identify temporal dependencies, tree-based ensemble algorithms, especially XGBoost, consistently deliver better results in terms of forecasting accuracy on structured retail demand datasets. A scalability case study on the Rossmann Store Sales benchmark evaluates the top-performing model on a larger, richer dataset. Moreover, the study shows the connection between forecast accuracy and the subsequent inventory performance by performing a cost-based evaluation of inventory outcomes of forecasts made using various models.

title: Polarization in sustainability disclosure: the role of accounting structural deviation and its impact on firm value and audit fees
summary: Purpose This paper aims to investigate the financial consequences of sustainability disclosure polarization, conceptualized as the structural departure of a firm’s reporting practices from industry norms toward opposite extremes. It aims to determine how polarization impacts firm value and audit fees and to unpack the underlying mechanisms of uncertainty and the effectiveness of the audit committee (AC) in an emerging market region. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a quantitative approach, this study analyzes a panel dataset of 2,235 firm-year observations from listed companies across major ASEAN economies. Structural equation modeling is used to test a moderated-mediation framework. This methodology examines the complex pathways linking polarization to firm value and audit fees, accounting for country-specific heterogeneities and proxy sensitivity. Simultaneously, it assesses the contingent effects of uncertainty and AC effectiveness. Findings The results reveal a non-linear, inverted U-shaped relationship between the level of disclosure polarization and firm value, suggesting an optimal point of strategic differentiation exists. The study finds that disclosure polarization is positively associated with higher audit fees. These relationships are significantly mediated by environmental uncertainty, although these main effects exhibit conditionality across different national contexts within the region. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the AC is found to negatively moderate (weaken) the adverse impact of polarization on audit fees. Practical implications The findings offer actionable insights for managers to pursue an optimal, rather than maximal, disclosure strategy focused on quality to enhance firm value and control costs. For boards, it highlights the tangible financial benefit of investing in an effective AC. For ASEAN regulators, it suggests that policy should prioritize disclosure quality and comparability over mere quantity to foster market confidence. Originality/value By empirically operationalizing disclosure polarization through the structural deviation of reporting quality and governance from industry medians, this research moves beyond simplistic linear views of sustainability reporting. It contributes an integrated empirical model explaining both valuation and cost consequences through the dual lenses of external uncertainty and internal governance. The findings offer actionable insights for managers on optimizing disclosure quality and for regulators on fostering market confidence in emerging economies.

title: Concilier valeurs, collaboration et supply chain : le cas d’une entreprise engagée
summary: Cette étude de cas analyse la manière dont Founty, une PME à mission créée en 2023, met en œuvre la collaboration au sein de sa supply chain en mobilisant des valeurs de durabilité, d’inclusion sociale et d’empowerment. La méthodologie repose sur une étude de cas qualitative fondée sur des entretiens semi-directifs complétés par des données secondaires. Les résultats mettent en évidence trois dimensions interdépendantes (valeurs, supply chain et collaboration) dont les interactions structurent la dynamique de la chaîne. Sur le plan théorique, l’étude contribue à la littérature sur le Sustainable Supply Chain Management en proposant un modèle d’articulation entre valeurs organisationnelles, pratiques collaboratives et structuration de la supply chain dans le contexte des PME à mission. Sur le plan managérial, elle met en évidence l’importance de l’alignement des valeurs dans la construction des partenariats et souligne le rôle des interactions collaboratives dans la gestion des contraintes opérationnelles d’une supply chain durable.

title: Reversing the role of the customer: the new ‘customer-as-a-supplier’ supply chain principle for the circular context
summary: This paper evaluates the relevance and sufficiency of a suite of six established supply chain principles for uncertainty reduction in circular supply chains, focusing on plastics in the construction sector. Using a structured intervention-based research approach, two trials with industry consortia designed and implemented closed-loop models for mortar tubs and aggregate packaging, incorporating higher recycled content and new reverse logistics arrangements. Findings confirm that original principles remain relevant but insufficient in circular contexts. We propose an additional principle ‘Customer-as-a-Supplier (CaaS)’ to address uncertainties in quality, timing, and volume of returned materials, and the changing role of customers in closed loop supply chains. CaaS emphasises communication, incentives, convenient return logistics, contamination control, and retailer engagement to enable high-quality material recovery. This extends the existing framework and highlights the active, and changing, role of customers. Future research should test the generality of CaaS and existing principles across diverse closed-loop supply chains.

title: The Multiple Economic Value of Information in the Digital Economy: Toward a multidimensional framework for information, and artificial intelligence
summary: In the digital economy information has taken on the role of a key economic resource, even though its economic value does not have to be the same as its market price. The body of work in information economics has provided a number of important but mostly separate explanations of information asymmetry, uncertainty reduction, signaling, property rights, pricing, network effects, organizational information and intangible capital. The present paper looks at these contributions again by means of a qualitative, theory-focused review of the literature referred to in the source text and puts forward an integrative interpretation of informational value. It is argued that information should be regarded as a multidimensional economic resource whose value can at the same time include aspects relating to use, exchange, organization, network, social and temporal dimensions. Market price is thus only one possible form of informational value and not a complete measure of it. The digital economy makes this distinction more apparent since digital information can be copied and distributed at a very low marginal cost, can produce consumer and network benefits which are not entirely reflected in transactions, and can at the same time act as both a private asset and a shared resource. Artificial intelligence enhances these features by increasing the scale, speed and complexity of information processing. The paper does not assert that economics as a whole is inadequate; instead it maintains that the various theories of information should be taken into account together when the economic value generated by information as a whole is the object of analysis.

title: Digitalization and Environmental, Social, and Governance Reporting: Evidence from the US Banking Industry
summary: ABSTRACT We examine the relation between digitalization and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting using a sample of listed US banks from 2010 to 2022. Our study is based on a two‐step theoretical framework, building on voluntary disclosure and signaling theory: First, we expect and find technological progress to enhance internal information quality. Second, we examine whether banks pass on this improved information to stakeholders via ESG reports. Our results suggest that banks are more likely to disclose an ESG report as they become more digitalized. Further, we find that digitalization is related to a higher extent and quality of ESG reporting. A difference‐in‐differences test and a mediation analysis corroborate our findings. Cross‐sectional tests indicate an attenuated association between digitalization and ESG reporting for banks with low data privacy and security disclosure. Our findings have practical implications because they highlight the potential of digitalization to improve ESG reporting but also possible drawbacks as digitalization comes along with certain risks.

title: Beyond conventional ESG: configurational synergies and path effects on the return resilience of infrastructure REITs
summary: As sustainable development has gained increasing prominence, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues have become an important research topic in the field of infrastructure real estate investment trusts (Infra-REITs). However, the three conventional ESG dimensions alone are no longer sufficient to fully explain the mechanisms through which ESG affects earnings resilience. Drawing on the operational characteristics of the Infra-REITs market, this study develops an “ESG+” analytical framework comprising two dimensions: underlying assets and capital markets. Using both questionnaire evidence and empirical data, it integrates fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) and necessary-condition analysis (NCA) to systematically identify the configurational paths through which multiple factors jointly shape the earnings resilience of Infra-REITs. To mitigate potential subjective bias, a LASSO regression model is further employed to identify key variables containing incremental predictive information and to conduct a complementary comparison with the configurational results. The results show that: (1) ESG elements such as green certification, energy efficiency, and social responsibility significantly enhance return resilience under specific contextual conditions, demonstrating strong multi-factor synergies; (2) project cash flow and energy efficiency emerge as core conditions across several configurations, underscoring the foundational role of operational performance in shaping Infra-REITs’ resilience; and (3) under imperfect legal and fiscal systems, market liquidity, pricing mechanisms, and information disclosure interact as critical complementary mechanisms that strengthen return stability. The findings contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of ESG–resilience linkages and provide theoretical and practical guidance for optimizing investment management and improving institutional design in the Infra-REITs market.

title: Digital transformation and third places: Mapping public spaces in Bekasi Regency
summary: As an urban and industrial area, Bekasi Regency faces challenges in providing inclusive and multifunctional public spaces that support social interaction, community cohesion, and economic activities. The limited availability of formal public spaces has encouraged the informal use of vacant spaces by local communities, indicating a need for both formal and informal “third places.” This study aims to develop a spatial database of third places in Bekasi Regency, identify their distribution patterns, and evaluate user experience through a phenomenological approach. A mixed-methods approach was applied by integrating Geographic Information System (GIS)-based spatial mapping using data scraped from Google Maps with field observations and semi-structured interviews at 24 purposively selected locations. The study identified 136 third places, classified into Civic/Public Spaces (33.8%), Commercial Social Spaces (40.4%), Spiritual/Communal Hubs (7.4%), and Hybrid/Productive Spaces (18.4%). These locations are mainly concentrated in the West Cikarang, North Cikarang, and South Tambun corridors. Reclassification showed that 75.7% of third places operate informally, indicating that community demand for social spaces is largely met outside the formal planning system. Internet connectivity was also found to influence space selection among migrant workers, younger people, and informal business operators. Differences in spatial quality were observed between developed commercial areas and densely populated residential and peri-urban areas. These findings highlight the need to recognize informal and hybrid spaces in the Bekasi Regency Detailed Spatial Plan (RDTR) and strengthen public digital infrastructure to support inclusive urban development.

title: Conceptual Mapping of Digital Transformation of Government Agencies: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Digital transformation in government agencies has become a major public sector reform agenda. However, existing academic studies remain conceptually fragmented across technological, organizational, and institutional perspectives. This study systematically maps the main concepts, interdimensional relationships, and dominant conceptual frameworks used to explain government digital transformation. It conducts a systematic literature review based on Kitchenham's protocol. It analyzes 30 reputable journal articles published between 2021 and 2025, sourced from Scopus, IEEE Xplore, SAGE Journals, Emerald Insight, and Taylor & Francis Online. The selection process was conducted in three stages and complemented by quality assessment to ensure methodological rigor. The findings show that government digital transformation is understood as multidimensional change in public organizations, involving the integration of digital technologies, changes in organizational structures and processes, institutional and governance influences, and orientation toward public value creation. However, relationships among these dimensions are generally treated implicitly and descriptively, without structured conceptual mapping. The literature is dominated by digital government evolution frameworks, co-evolutionary models, and public value frameworks, but these perspectives remain weakly integrated. This study contributes by developing an integrated conceptual mapping that clarifies the structure of knowledge and the interdimensional relationships in government digital transformation, serving as a basis for theoretical development and future research.

title: Anchoring in the Storm: How Does Digital Intelligence Technology Foster Green Innovation Resilience?
summary: Abstract In an era characterized by dual transformations and climate-induced turbulence, manufacturing firms are compelled to shift their strategic paradigm from static "green growth" to dynamic "green survival." Based on data from Chinese A-share manufacturing listed companies from 2012 to 2023, this study empirically examines the impact mechanisms and boundary conditions of digital intelligence technology on green innovation resilience. The findings indicate that: (1) Digital intelligence technology significantly enhances the green innovation resilience of manufacturing firms. (2) Mechanism tests reveal that digital intelligence technology empowers green innovation resilience through a dual pathway of alleviating financing constraints and improving managerial efficiency. (3) Climate risk attention plays a critical moderating role in this process; specifically, it significantly enhances the marginal contributions of financing constraint alleviation and managerial efficiency improvement to green innovation resilience. (4) Heterogeneity analysis shows that the empowering effect is more pronounced in non-high-tech, non-heavy-polluting, and high-competition industries, as well as in Eastern-based, non-labor-intensive, and upstream firms. This study reveals that only by achieving strategic alignment between digital capabilities and subjective risk perception can firms effectively coordinate resources to maintain green innovation resilience.

title: Supply Chain Readiness and Food Security in Dryland Environments: Empirical Evidence from Kenya’s Arid and Semi-Arid Land Counties
summary: Agri-food distribution networks operating across dryland regions face intense operational disruptions caused by extreme climate shocks, infrastructural vulnerabilities, and rapid market fluctuations. This study examines the empirical effect of Supply Chain Readiness Strategy on food security outcomes across Kenya’s 29 Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) counties. Theoretical anchoring is established through Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT)—specifically focusing on sensing and seizing capabilities—and Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) Theory. Supply chain readiness was operationalised through three key indicators: early-warning surveillance systems, pre-formulated emergency response protocols, and rapid logistics mobilisation capabilities. Utilising an explanatory cross-sectional survey design grounded in a pragmatic philosophical framework, primary empirical data were collected from a census of County Directors of Agriculture and Crop Production Officers (N=29; 100% response rate). Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was conducted for data reduction, extracting a single dominant component that accounted for 81.20% of total variance. Binary logistic regression and marginal effects estimations were employed to test the underlying hypothesis. Empirical findings revealed that supply chain readiness exerts a statistically significant positive effect on food security (β= 1.624, p = 0.028). The calculated odds ratio (β= 5.073) demonstrates that ASAL counties with structured readiness strategies are over five times more likely to maintain stable food security conditions than those with low readiness capabilities. Marginal effects estimation showed that a unit increase in readiness increases the probability of achieving food security by 25.1 percentage points (dy/dx = 0.251, p = 0.032). The study concludes that proactive early-warning surveillance, pre-allocated emergency funds, and rapid deployment protocols are essential drivers of food availability and market stability in volatile dryland ecosystems. Devolved county governments and humanitarian agencies are urged to institutionalise predictive surveillance systems and pre-approved logistics contingency frameworks.

title: Accounting Information Entropy, Resilience, and Economic Transmission: A Theory of Market and Capital-Allocation Responses to Information Shocks
summary: Accounting information constitutes a critical informational infrastructure through which economic agents coordinate expectations, evaluate firms, allocate capital, and respond to uncertainty. Existing accounting research has extensively examined information quality, disclosure, information asymmetry, and capital-market consequences, but comparatively less attention has been devoted to the dynamic transmission of accounting information disturbances across interconnected economic agents. This paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding how accounting information shocks generate entropy, how that entropy propagates through economic networks, and how accounting information resilience moderates the magnitude, speed, and persistence of economic transmission. Building on the Accounting Information Entropy–Resilience Theory (AIERT), the paper conceptualizes accounting information entropy as a state variable representing informational disorder generated by uncertainty, inconsistency, ambiguity, reporting disruption, and reduced information precision. The framework proposes that information shocks can propagate through ownership, financing, supply-chain, investment, and market networks. Accounting information resilience acts as a stabilizing capacity by limiting shock amplification, accelerating information recovery, and reducing the persistence of economically relevant uncertainty. The paper develops a dynamic transmission model in which an initial accounting information disturbance produces changes in entropy, information frictions, expectations, financing conditions, asset prices, and capital allocation. It introduces the concepts of informational shock amplification, entropy persistence, resilience-adjusted transmission, and economic transmission elasticity. The framework further predicts nonlinear propagation, threshold effects, asymmetric recovery, and network-dependent contagion. A comprehensive empirical research architecture is proposed using panel models, event studies, network models, spatial specifications, differencein-differences designs, dynamic panel estimators, and quasi-experimental identification strategies. The paper contributes to accounting and economics by extending the analysis of accounting information from firm-level quality toward dynamic economic transmission. It argues that the economic importance of accounting information depends not only on its accuracy or relevance but also on its ability to prevent, absorb, and recover from informational shocks that propagate through interconnected economic systems.

title: Climate finance, innovation, and the low-carbon transition in Portugal: Evidence from a nonlinear ARDL approach
summary: Balancing economic development with environmental sustainability remains a critical challenge for many European economies pursuing low-carbon transitions. Although Portugal has made substantial progress in renewable energy deployment and technological innovation, the environmental impacts of economic growth, urbanization, and trade openness remain complex. They may exhibit asymmetric responses to policy and market shocks. Therefore, this study investigates the asymmetric and dynamic relationships among urbanization (URB), trade openness (TRD), economic growth (EG), renewable energy (RE), innovation (INNO), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in Portugal using the Nonlinear Autoregressive Distributed Lag (NARDL) framework. Annual time-series data covering the period 1990–2023 were employed to examine both long-run and short-run asymmetries in the environmental effects of these macroeconomic factors. The empirical findings reveal that positive shocks in EG and URB significantly increase CO₂ emissions, whereas increases in RE consumption and INNO substantially reduce environmental degradation. TRD exhibits mixed effects; while trade expansion initially increases emissions through higher production activity, it contributes to long-run emissions reductions through technology diffusion and cleaner trade composition. The results further indicate that negative shocks to RE and INNO have disproportionately adverse environmental consequences, highlighting the fragility of sustainability gains. These findings demonstrate Portugal’s progress in aligning economic development with RE transition and INN-driven climate strategies. The study provides novel evidence on the asymmetric effects of economic and policy shocks on environmental quality. It offers policy recommendations that support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 9, 11, and 13.

title: Adaptation Versus Mitigation Climate Finance and Ecological Footprint in Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence from Method of Moments Quantile Regression
summary: Climate finance to Sub-Saharan Africa has grown, yet the region's ecological footprint continues to exceed its biocapacity. Most studies treat climate finance as a single aggregate and estimate average effects. This study asks whether adaptation and mitigation finance affect ecological pressure differently and whether their effects vary between low-footprint and high-footprint countries. Using a panel of 48 Sub-Saharan African countries over 2010 to 2022, it measures adaptation and mitigation finance as disbursements per capita from the OECD Climate-Related Development Finance database and ecological footprint per capita from the National Footprint and Biocapacity Accounts. After tests for cross-sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, unit roots and cointegration, the study applies the Method of Moments Quantile Regression, tests the equality of the two finance coefficients at each quantile, and separates the carbon and land-based footprint components. Mitigation finance reduces the ecological footprint, with effects that grow toward the upper quantiles, whereas adaptation finance reduces it mainly at the lower and middle quantiles. The two effects differ significantly at the tails of the distribution. The findings support allocating each stream according to a country's position in the footprint distribution.
